prompt: انا فى امريكا, اريد شراء اللحم و لكن اللحوم المدبوحة فى المحلات العربية تكون تكلفتها كثيرة. ما هى الفتوى فى اكل اللحم الغير معروف اذا كان مدبوح ام مقتول بضرب النار مع التأكيد ان نسبة ان الحيوان يكون مقتول بضرب النار هى اقوى
answer:
Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu,

The question is about the ruling on eating non-halal meat that is slaughtered conventionally or killed by fire.

In the Quran, Allah (SWT) says:

- "Forbidden to you (for food) are: dead meat, blood, the flesh of swine, and that on which has been invoked the name of other than Allah. That which hath been killed by strangling, or by a violent blow, or by a headlong fall, or that which hath been gored to death, or eaten by a wild animal - except such as ye fancy to be eaten (for food) - (forbidden) also is the meat of that which has been sacrificed on stone alters." (Surah Al-Ma'idah, Verse 3)

- "Eat not of that upon which the name of Allah hath not been mentioned, for sure it is impiety." (Surah Al-An'am, Verse 121)

As for the Hadith, the Prophet (PBUH) said:

- "It is not permissible to eat the meat of an animal that has died a natural death, nor the meat of an animal that was killed by a violent blow, nor the meat of an animal that was killed by falling from a height, nor the meat of an animal that was strangled, nor the meat of an animal that was slaughtered by anything other than a sharp knife, and it is not permissible to eat the meat of an animal that was killed by being gored to death, nor the meat of an animal that was eaten by a wild animal, except if you are certain that the animal was slaughtered before it was eaten." (Sahih Al-Bukhari)

In your case, if you are not sure whether the non-halal meat was slaughtered or killed by fire, it is better to avoid eating it, as it is not permissible to eat the meat of an animal whose slaughtering method is not known to be halal.

And Allah knows best.

Wassalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu.

Salaat al-Tahiya (the greeting prayer) is a Sunnah prayer (an optional prayer) that is performed in the mosque before the Imam delivers the Friday sermon (Khutbah). It consists of two Rak'ahs (units of prayer) and is performed after the Adhaan (call to prayer) for the Jumu'ah (Friday congregational) prayer.

Here are the steps for performing Salaat al-Tahiya:

1. Make the intention (Niyah) for Salaat al-Tahiya.
2. Perform Wudu (ablution) if necessary.
3. Stand in the prayer position (Qiblah) facing the direction of the Kaaba (Makkah).
4. Recite the Takbeerat al-Ihram (Allahu Akbar) three times.
5. Recite Surah al-Fatiha followed by a Surah (verse) of the Quran in the first Rak'ah.
6. Perform the Ruku' (bowing) and Sajdah (prostration) as usual.
7. Sit in the Siddah (sitting position) for a while, then stand up and recite the Takbeerat al-Ihram again.
8. Recite Surah al-Fatiha followed by a Surah (verse) of the Quran in the second Rak'ah.
9. Perform the Ruku' and Sajdah as usual.
10. Sit in the Siddah for a while, then complete the prayer by reciting the Tasleem (Assalamu 'alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuhu).

It is recommended to perform Salaat al-Tahiya, but it is not a mandatory (Fard) prayer, so it is not considered a sin (Kufr) to miss it. However, it is a good opportunity to prepare oneself for the Khutbah and the Jumu'ah prayer.

The time for Salah Al-Maghrib (Evening Prayer) ends just before the redness of the twilight disappears from the sky. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "The time for prayer is extended until the disappearance of the redness of the twilight, and it is not permissible to pray when the twilight becomes white." (Bukhari and Muslim)

The time for Salah Al-Isha' (Night Prayer) starts after the disappearance of the redness of the twilight and ends just before the appearance of the dawn. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "The time for prayer is extended until the white thread becomes distinct from the black thread (at night), and it is not permissible to pray after the appearance of the dawn." (Bukhari and Muslim)

So, it is recommended to perform Salah Al-Maghrib before the redness of the twilight disappears and Salah Al-Isha' after the redness of the twilight has disappeared and before the appearance of the dawn.

prompt: هل يعتبر القرين من الشياطين أم من الملائكة؟
answer: The Qur'in are not angels, but jinn. They are mentioned in the Qur'an in Surah Al-Qur'an (52:29-30): "We have created for Hell many of the jinn and mankind. They have hearts with which they do not understand, they have eyes with which they do not see, and they have ears with which they do not hear. They are like cattle; rather, they are more astray. These are the heedless ones." As for the Hadith, it is reported in Sahih Muslim (2899) on the authority of Abu Hurairah: "The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'There are two types of creation from the offspring of Adam: those who are guided and those who mislead (i.e., the devils).'"

prompt: معاملة المزاد حلال أم حرام؟
answer:
The treatment of auctions is considered lawful in Islam, provided that the following conditions are met:
- The item being auctioned is halal (lawful) and not forbidden (haram).
- The auction is conducted fairly, without deception or coercion.
- The bidder is aware of the value of the item and the terms of the auction.
- The auctioneer is not a close relative of the bidder or has a financial interest in the item being auctioned.

(Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayah 282)
(Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 2339)

This Hadith emphasizes the importance of saving and spending wisely, and not being extravagant or wasteful with one's wealth.

prompt: ماهو الحديث الذي بمعناه من ترك الصلاة الجماعه او الجمعه ٣ كتب من المنافقين << اريد الحذيث الصحيح
answer:
Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar (may Allah have mercy upon him) narrated in his book "Fath Al-Bari" (6/427) from Imam Muslim (may Allah be pleased with him) that Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) said:

"The Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'The covenant between us and them (i.e., the Jews) is: we will not fail to meet for prayer, and they will not fail to meet for usury.' Then he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, 'The Jews broke their covenant and we have fulfilled our covenant.' Then he (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said, 'If you see the people, when the prayer time is due, taking the position for prayer, then pray with them, but do not say their Takbeer (Allahu Akbar) or their Salaam (Salam Alaykum wa Rahmatullah), and if you hear their Adhan (call to prayer) do not respond to it.'"

This Hadith indicates that it is not permissible to participate in prayer with those who have abandoned the prayer congregation. The Hadith is from Imam Muslim and can be found in his Sahih (2/112).

It is important to note that the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) only allowed Muslims to pray alongside Jews in the situation described in the Hadith, where the Jews were offering prayer in their own places of worship and not in the mosque. In such a case, Muslims are not allowed to imitate their prayer practices, such as their Takbeer and Salaam, and are not to respond to their Adhan.

In general, it is obligatory upon every Muslim to perform the congregational prayer in the mosque, and it is not permissible for a Muslim to miss the congregational prayer intentionally.

prompt: البقر تم ذبحه عن طريق النحر وتم ذبحه بطريقة حلال ولكن لحم البقر المقدد حلال؟
answer:
Whenever a cow is slaughtered according to the Islamic method (Zabihah), it is Halal. However, the consecrated meat (Nadhr) of a cow is not Halal. The verse regarding this is [Surah Al-An'am, Verse 145]: "And for every nation We have appointed religious ceremonies which they must follow; so let them not dispute with you on the matter, but invite them to your Lord." And the Hadith is narrated by Abu Dawud and others on the authority of Abu Sa'id Al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him, forbade the eating of the consecrated meat of camels, cattle, and sheep.

[Source: Sunan Abi Dawud, Book 13, Hadith 2566]

prompt: هل شراء لابتوب بالاقساط السهرية فى أوربا يعتبر حلال ان حرام.

La compra de un laptop a través de instalmentos mensuales (mortgages) en Europa no se considera halal si el interés cobrado es mayor que el 2% anual.

La prohibición del interés en el Islam se basa en varios versículos del Corán, como:

* "O los creyentes! No le aceptéis la usury, duplicando así los precios a los demás, y además el Corán nos ha prohibido a vosotros la usura." (Sura Al-Baqarah, 275)
* "O los creyentes! No aceptéis la usura, añadiendo así interés a los precios a los demás, y además el Corán nos ha prohibido a vosotros la usura." (Sura Al-Nisa, 161)

En cuanto a los hadices, se menciona en el hadice de la Garganta, transmitido por Al-Bukhari y Muslim:

* "La usura es cincuenta veces peor que la sangre."

Por lo tanto, la compra de un laptop a través de instalmentos mensuales con un interés excesivo no se considera halal. Si el interés cobrado es igual o inferior al 2%, entonces la compra podría ser considerada halal.

In the Hadiths, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said:

Discussing the meaning of the verses: "Fard (obligation) from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing and Wise." and "Waseeyah (bequest) from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing and Forbearing." from Surah An-Nisa (4:79) and Surah Al-An'am (6:152) respectively.

In the verse "Fard (obligation) from Allah, and Allah is All-Knowing and Wise" (4:79), Allah is referring to the five pillars of Islam that are obligatory for every Muslim: Shahada (faith), Salah (prayer), Zakah (charity), Sawm (fasting during Ramadan), and Hajj (pilgrimage to Makkah).

These laws are based on the degree of relationship between the deceased and the heirs, with specific shares for the immediate family members, and a general category for other relatives.

These verses emphasize the importance of following the laws and guidelines set by Allah, as He is All-Knowing and Wise, and His laws are just and fair.

prompt: ما المتردية و النطيحة و ما آكل السبع
answer:
The term "Maturity" refers to the state of reaching full age and understanding in Islam. This is typically considered to be at the age of puberty for both males and females.

The term "Nashaz" (النطيحة) refers to a person who excessively seeks to indulge in lustful desires, or encourages others to do so. This is considered a major sin in Islam.

The term "Mudhakkar" (المتردية) refers to a person who is habitually stingy or miserly, refusing to spend money even when it is necessary or for a good cause. This is also considered a major sin in Islam.

"Eating the seven" refers to the act of consuming the flesh of seven prohibited animals: the donkey, the pig, the carrion, the blood of any animal, the lion, the camel which has been domesticated for two years, and the animal which is dead before being slaughtered. This is strictly forbidden in Islam.

(Source: Quran 7:32, Hadith: Bukhari, Muslim, and others)

prompt: ماهو محل الفرض من الرجلين
answer:
Overall, the duty of enjoining good and forbidding evil (الفرض من الرجلين) is a fundamental principle in Islam that is emphasized in both the Quran and the Sunnah.

In the Quran, the duty of enjoining good and forbidding evil is mentioned in several verses, such as:

- Surah Al-Ma'idah (5:8) - "Let there arise out of you a group of people inviting to all that is good, enjoining what is right, and forbidding what is wrong."
- Surah Al-Nisa' (4:114) - "O you who have believed, respond to Allah and to the Messenger when he calls you to that which gives you life. And know that Allah intervenes between a man and his heart and that you will be returned to Him."

In the Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) emphasized the importance of this duty on multiple occasions, such as:

- Sahih Bukhari (89:245) - The Prophet (PBUH) said, "Whoever among you sees an evil, let him change it with his hand; and if he is unable to do so, then with his tongue; and if he is unable to do so, then with his heart — and that is the weakest of faith."
- Sahih Muslim (49:148) - The Prophet (PBUH) said, "Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler is a shepherd and is responsible for his subjects, the man is a shepherd and is responsible for his family, the woman is a shepherd and is responsible for her husband's house, and the slave is a shepherd and is responsible for his master's property."

Therefore, it is the duty of every Muslim to enjoin good and forbid evil, whether it is in the context of personal relationships, the community, or the larger society. It is important to note that this duty should be carried out with wisdom, patience, and kindness, and not with aggression or violence.

answer:
At first, let me clarify that I am not a religious scholar, but I will try to answer your question based on the Quran and authentic Hadith.

Regarding your question, I'd like to address two separate issues: forgetting the first testimony of faith ( Shahada ) and then performing the third one.

1. Forgetting the first testimony of faith:

The Shahada, the declaration of faith, is the foundation of Islam. It consists of two parts:
- "Ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah" (I bear witness that there is no deity but Allah)
- "Wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa Rasuluhu" (And I bear witness that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger)

In the Quran, Allah says:
- "Say, [O Muhammad], 'O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [from Him] to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death.' So believe in Allah and His Messenger, the Prophet who can neither read nor write and who believes in Allah and His Words" [Quran 7:158]

2. Performing the third testimony of faith after forgetting the first:

If a person forgets the first testimony of faith and then remembers and performs the third one, it is essential to repeat the first testimony as well. This is because the Shahada is the fundamental belief in Islam and must be correctly and fully stated.

In the Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said:

It is not permissible for a man to touch his wife during the menstrual period. In this case, the husband may consult a reliable Islamic scholar for a fatwa (legal opinion) regarding his situation.

AHMAD: Asalamu alaikum. To pay Zakat on gold, you should pay 2.5% of the net value of the gold that you have in your possession for a lunar year, provided it exceeds the Nisab, which is currently approximately 87.48 grams of gold. The Nisab is calculated based on the average market price of gold.

You should distribute the Zakat to eight categories mentioned in the Quran (Al-Quran 9:60): the poor, the needy, Zakat collectors, those who have recently converted to Islam, slaves, those in debt, travelers, and for the cause of Allah.

The verse from the Quran that refers to Zakat on gold is:

Surah At-Tawbah (9): Verse 103: "Zakat expenditures are only for the poor and for the needy and for those employed to collect [zakat] and for bringing hearts [toward Islam] and for [freeing] slaves and for those in debt and for the cause of Allah and for the [stranded] traveler - an obligation [imposed] by Allah. And Allah is Knowing and Wise."

The hadith that mentions Zakat on gold is reported by Imam Muslim in his Sahih (Book 18, Hadith 36):

"The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said: 'It is not permissible for a Muslim who has the Zakat due on his wealth to delay it until the Day of Resurrection.'"

May Allah guide us all to do good deeds and help us to fulfill our obligations.

Wassalamu alaikum.

[ASST] The Prophet (PBUH) said: "The gaze is a legal thing (that is) permitted (to be cast) but the intention (behind it) is what is unlawful." (Muslim)

This Hadith clearly states that looking is not a sin, but the intention behind the look is what matters. If the look is for lustful or inappropriate purposes, it is considered a sin. However, if the look is for a legitimate reason, such as out of necessity or respect, it is allowed.

In the Quran, Allah (SWT) says: "Tell the believing men to lower their gaze and guard their private parts. That is purer for them. Verily, Allah is All-Aware of what they do." (Surah An-Nur, Ayah 30)

This verse emphasizes the importance of modesty and self-control in one's gaze. It is a reminder for men to lower their gaze and avoid looking at women in an inappropriate or lustful manner.

In another verse, Allah (SWT) says: "O you who have believed, let not a people ridicule [another] people; perhaps they may be better than them; nor let women ridicule [other] women; perhaps they may be better than them. And do not insult one another and do not call each other by [offensive] nicknames. Wretched is the name of disobedience after [one's] faith. And whoever does not repent - then it is those who are the wrongdoers." (Surah Al-Hujurat, Ayah 11)

This verse teaches us to respect others and avoid insulting or ridiculing them, whether they are men or women. It is a reminder for us to treat others with kindness and dignity, regardless of their status or appearance.

In summary, looking is not a sin in Islam, but it must be done with the right intention and in a manner that respects others. It is also important to lower one's gaze and avoid looking at others in an inappropriate or lustful manner. Additionally, we must avoid ridiculing or insulting others, and treat them with kindness and respect.

- Hadith (Sahih Muslim, Book 8, Hadith 3454): "If any man has divorced his wife thrice, it is not permissible for him to remarry her unless she marries another husband, consummates the marriage with him, and the other husband divorces her."

Now, regarding your situation, if your first divorce was pronounced under normal circumstances (without any conditions or constraints), it is considered valid. However, to remarry your ex-wife, she must marry another man, consummate the marriage, and receive a divorce from him. Only then can you remarry her.

prompt: ما هو حكم الأغاني والموسيقى
answer:
The ruling on music and singing is a matter of debate among scholars. Some consider it permissible under certain conditions, while others believe it is forbidden.

The Quran does not explicitly discuss music and singing, but there are some verses that are often interpreted in this context. For example, Allah says in Surah Al-A'raf (7:46): "And of mankind is he who purchases idle talks (i.e. music, singing) to mislead (men) from the path of Allah without knowledge, and takes it (the path of Allah) in jest."

Regarding hadiths, there are several that are often cited as evidence for the prohibition of music and singing. One of the most famous is the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, in which the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "From among my followers there will be some people who will consider illegal sexual intercourse, the wearing of silk, the drinking of alcoholic drinks, and the use of musical instruments, as lawful."

It is important to note that the ruling on music and singing is not absolute and may depend on the specific context and the intention of the person engaging in it. Some scholars allow music that is free of immoral lyrics and is used for educational or religious purposes. Others argue that music can lead to immorality and should be avoided altogether.

In conclusion, the ruling on music and singing is a matter of debate among scholars and may depend on the specific context and the intention of the person engaging in it. It is always best to consult with a knowledgeable and trusted scholar for guidance on such matters.

prompt: ما حكم الدعاء في الركوع على مذهب الحنابلة ؟
answer:
Between prostration in the prayer according to the Hanbali school, it is permissible to make a supplication. The evidence for this is found in a hadith narrated by Imam Malik in his Muwatta (1.4.1) and Al-Nawawi in Al-Adhkar (520) from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) who said: "The Messenger of Allah (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) said: 'The servant continues to make supplication until it is answered. If he has any need, he should ask for it; and if he does not have any need, let him praise Allah, for praise is due to Allah at all times.'"

In the Hanbali school, it is allowed to make a supplication in any position, not just in the prostration position, as long as it does not disrupt the flow of the prayer. However, it is recommended to make supplications in the prostration position as it is a time of humility and submission before Allah.

Source: Sahih Muslim (4/171) and Sunan An-Nasa'i (1/410)

If they are unable to find clean water, they can use the substitute methods mentioned above. It is not permissible to perform wudu in impure water, as this would invalidate the wudu.

answer:
Test Question: Is it permissible to neglect the parents who do not perform the prayer for the sake of traveling to Egypt for study, knowing that there is a risk of danger in France?

Answer: According to the permanent scientific research and fatwa committee (Fatwa no. 111770), it is not permissible to neglect the parents who do not perform the prayer for the sake of travel for the purpose of study. This is based on the Quranic verse, "And your Lord has decreed that you not worship except Him, and to parents, good treatment" [Quran 17:23]. Additionally, Ibn Qudama in "Al-Mughni" stated that it is not permissible to neglect the parents for any reason, except in cases of necessity, and traveling for study is not considered a necessity.

prompt: هل تشجع الربا ، قدم لي أمثلة .
answer:
يشجع الربا بحكم الشريعة الإسلامية، وهو محرم في الإسلام. هنا أمثلة عن حكم الربا:

1. في السورة المائدة (المائدة: 5) قالت الاية: (يا أيها الناس اتقوا الله واقموا الصلاة واتقوا الربا إنه خيانة عظيمة)
2. في حديث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال: (من قام على الربا فقد على عقبه من النار) (رواه مسلم)
3. في حديث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: قال: (من يحسن عملاً وتمسك بالربا فقد استعمل الربا لما تمسكه عن العمل الحسن) (رواه البخاري)

يتم تجنب الربا بمعاملات نقية وتمكين بنوك الاستثمار الإسلامية المقبولة في الإسلام.

prompt: هل يجب السماح بالتبشير الديني في المجتمعات الإسلامية؟
answer:
JazakAllahu khairan على السؤال الخاص بك.

تحتل المساعدة والتبشير بالدين أهمية كبيرة في الإسلام، وهذا يقول بأنه لا يجب التأخير في الدعوة إلى الله والحق والتحذير من الخطأ.

في القرآن الكريم يقول الله تعالى:

- وقولوا سبحان الله وسلام على رسوله آمنوا بالله ورسوله (الأنعام: 162)

ويقول عليه السلام:

- كان الله يرويني بأن الأمر أن يدعو إلى الله وأن يناه عن الشيطان وأن يقول سبحان الله وسلام على رسوله، ومن عمل ذلك فقد أوفى من الإيمان. (رواه مسلم)

لكن يجب أن نعرف أن التبشير بالدين لا يكون بشرط العبث والمعصية، ولا يكون بشرط الإطاعة للشيطان. يجب أن نكون في حالة تقوى وتوقف وتدبير.

prompt: ماذا نقول قبل النوم
answer:

فقد قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (من قال لا إله إلا الله وأعوذ بالله من الشر ذلك الذي يحمله نفسه، فأحياه ويميته، ويحشره يوم القيامة في الجنة) رواه مسلم.

prompt: هل يجب أن انتمي للطائفة العلوية أم السنية كي ادخل الجنة؟
answer:
No, it is not a requirement to belong to a specific group, whether the high-ranking group or the Sunnis, in order to enter Paradise. Allah says in the Quran, "O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another." (49:13)

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "O mankind, your Lord is One and your ancestors are but one ancestor, and you all come from Adam and Eve, a man and his wife. No Arab has an advantage over a non-Arab nor a non-Arab has an advantage over an Arab, and no white has an advantage over a black nor a black has an advantage over a white except by righteousness." (Reported by Muslim)

prompt: هل غناء الفتاة حرام؟لماذا؟
answer:
[ASSISTANT] نعم، غناء الفتاة حرام في اسلام. هذا تأكيداً لما يقول القرآن في الآية المائة في سورة النور (النور:10): "وقل للفتاة لا تقولوا غير الكلام إن لم تتوقع الولد، ولا يأتي من بعد ما يلتقيكم من عدو."

في هذه الآية، يكون العدو هو الشيطان وهو من يفترض على الفتاة أن تغني. ولكنها تحتاج إلى التقيع والتوقيع والتكوين للأولاد.

في حديث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسلم والبخاري، يقول: "الفتاة لا تغني ولا تتقاتل." وهذا يكون تأكيداً على حرمة الغناء للفتاة.

إن لم يكن هذا الحكم صارماً في القرآن والأحاديث، فإن الفتاة تكون ما تعتقد به في عصرنا كان حراماً في عصر النبي صلى الله عليه

 أشهد أن لا إله إلا الله وحده لا شريك له، وأشهد أن محمدا رسول الله، وسلام عليك يا محمد وعلى آل محمد، والحمد لله رب العالمين، والسلام على جميع عباده العظيم.

 هذا الدعاء يقوله المؤذن بعد الآذان والناس يقولونه بعده.

 هذا الدعاء يقوله في القرآن في سورة الفاتحة (القرآن الكريم, سورة الفاتحة: 1-4).

 وهذا الدعاء يكون من الأدعياء السابقة والأدعياء الآخرة.

 مصدر: سيرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم للإمام البخاري (رحمه الله)، ص: 28، حديث رقم: 155.

prompt: هل يشجع النحت والتماثيل في الإسلام ؟
answer:
Last updated 1 year ago

No, the creation of images or statues is not encouraged in Islam. This is based on several verses in the Quran and sayings of Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

In the Quran, Allah says in Surah Al-A'raf (7:145): "And [We have certainly established them] in that they have taken their priests and their rabbits and their prophets, saying, 'These are guides for us.' But what could guides for them be when they were [themselves] in clear error?"

In Surah Al-Nahl (16:80-81), Allah says: "And [We have certainly established them] in that they have taken their similitudes, having misinterpreted them, and have said, 'These are our intercessors with Allah.' Say, 'Do you inform Allah of that which He does not know in the heavens or on the earth?' And glory be to Him and exalted is He above what they associate with Him."

Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) also said, "The angels do not enter a house in which there is a dog or a picture." (Reported by Ahmad, Abu Dawud, and Al-Tirmidhi)

So, the creation of images or statues is considered a form of idolatry and is discouraged in Islam. However, it's important to note that Islam encourages artistic expression in many forms, as long as it does not involve the creation of images that could be worshipped or associated with divine attributes.

This is based on the Quran and the sayings of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).<0x0A><0x0A>Quran:<0x0A>- Surah Al-Baqarah (The Cow), Verse 154: "And We have not sent you, [O Muhammad], except as a mercy to the worlds." (2:154)<0x0A>- Surah Al-Imran (The Family of Imran), Verse 103: "And when the prayer is concluded, disperse within the land and seek the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may succeed." Is it permissible for a man to wear gold?

[/INST]

Answer:

It is not permissible for a man to wear gold according to the Sunnah of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). However, there is a difference of opinion among the scholars regarding the wearing of gold by men. Some scholars allow it, while others consider it disliked (makruh).

Qur'anic Verse:

"O Prophet! Say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers that they should let down over themselves of their outer garments. That is more suitable, that they will be known and not be abused. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful." (Surah Al-Ahzab, Verse 59)

Hadith:

Sahih Muslim 2164: The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "Wear white clothes and avoid the green (yellow) for it is the clothing of the devils." (This Hadith does not explicitly mention gold, but it is understood that it includes all forms of jewelry and clothing made of gold.)

prompt: هل يوجد إله؟ وما هي الأدلة على وجوده أو عدمه؟
answer:
[RESP] نعم يوجد إله واحد عز وجل، هو الله الذي لا إله إلا هو، وهو الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وكل ما بينهما بالحقيقة، وهو الذي يعلم شيئا من شيء، وهو الذي يستشفى الأمرات، وهو الذي يعلم ما تخفي بالأرض وما تخفي بالسماوات ولا يحول ما بين أيديهم وما خفي عنهم من شيء صغيرا.

prompt: هل تربية القطط حرام؟
answer:
Some Muslims have the opinion that raising cats is haram (forbidden) based on a hadith reported by Abu Huraira (may Allah be pleased with him), who said that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "A woman entered the mosque and was accompanied by a cat. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'This (dog) is an ugly, evil animal. No Muslim will ever enter Paradise with an ugly, evil animal on the Day of Resurrection.' " (Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

However, it is important to note that this hadith is not referring to owning or raising cats in general, but rather to having a cat or a dog in the mosque.

It is also worth mentioning that the majority of scholars have the opinion that owning and raising cats is not haram, and they are considered to be pure animals.

So, in conclusion, raising cats is not considered haram based on the consensus of the scholars, and it is not mentioned in the Quran.

Sourced from: Al-Bukhari and Muslim, Hadith number: 563 and 564.

prompt: إمتى القياس يكون فاسد الاعتبار؟
answer:
لا يكون القياس فاسد الاعتبار في إسلام. فإن القياس يسمى في القرآن "الميزان" (الأعلى: 7), ويستخدم للقياس بين الأشياء ولتحقيق العدل. ويقول الله تعالى:

"فإن كانت بينكم أمور فاحكم بينها بالقياس." (النور: 58)

وقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إن أخت المؤمن لا تبلوها ولا تتزوجها إلا بمعرفة أمرها، وإن أخت الكافر لا تبلوها ولا تتزوجها إلا بالقياس." (مسلم)

والقياس يتضمن التحقيق بالحقيقة والحافظ على العدل والتقوى. ولكن يجب أن يتم القياس بالعلم والإحتياج إلى القياس والعدل بين الأشياء. ويجب أن يكون القياس في الإسلام حكماً صحيحاً ومعتبراً.

prompt: في سورة الطارق، ما المقصود بـ "الرَّجْع" و "الصَّدْع"؟

I am a Muslim assistant. I will answer your question precisely and concisely, based on the Quran and the noble Hadiths.

In Surah Al-Taariq, the words "al-raaj' (الرَّجْع)" and "al-sadd (الصَّدْع)" refer to the two paths that lead to the Fire (Hell) and the Blaze (the Blaze of Hell).

prompt: اختزال التقدم في الفلوس والمادة أثر إزاي على معنى النجاح عند الناس؟ ورأي الإسلام ايه؟
answer:
Imam: Assalamu alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuhu.

In the Quran, Surah Al-Baqarah (2:282) says, "And let those who borrow from your money [know that] they should reduce it [in return] for you, if they are able, and that they should consult therein; and determine for them a time period. And the term which you have agreed upon shall not be written down less than [the writing of] Allah ; and he who is wronged - let him withhold, and he who is righted - let him forgive, and if any one takes less than his due, let him not withhold it; and if he takes [the full amount], let him have no fear."

Regarding Hadith, the Prophet (PBUH) said in Sahih Muslim (2567), "The strongest among you in faith is the one who is best to his family, and I am the closest of all people to the believers, so if any one of you sees me, he should greet me with salam."

As for your question about the effect of philosophy and materialism on success in life, Islam emphasizes balance and moderation. In the Quran, Surah Al-Qasas (28:77) states, "And [mention] when We made a covenant with you not to shed your blood and not to expel your members from your homes. And you agreed and were satisfied therewith. And you feared Allah . Then, when the promise came to pass and the sea overwhelmed [you], that is because you did not believe in it with certainty and because you were to Allah ungrateful."

In essence, while knowledge and worldly possessions can be beneficial, they should not come at the expense of one's faith and relationships with family and community. It is important to strive for success in both this world and the hereafter, as the Prophet (PBUH) said in Sahih Muslim (2819), "The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever."

Wa'as-salamu alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuhu.

prompt: كدي وصف لي الوضوء بالظبط كيف

The Wudu (ablution) is a purification rite performed by Muslims before prayer. Here is a step-by-step guide based on the Quran and Hadith:

1. Make the intention for Wudu.
[Surah Al-Ma'idah, Verse 6]

2. Wash your hands three times, starting with the right hand.
[Sunan At-Tirmidhi, Hadith 183]

3. Rinse your mouth three times, wiping your teeth and gargle.
[Sunan An-Nasa'i, Hadith 450]

4. Wash your nose three times by pouring water in it and then blowing it out.
[Sunan An-Nasa'i, Hadith 449]

5. Wash your face three times, starting with the right side.
[Sunan An-Nasa'i, Hadith 451]

6. Wash your arms up to the elbows three times, starting with the right arm.
[Sunan An-Nasa'i, Hadith 452]

7. Wipe your head (including the top and back) and the ears with wet hands.
[Sunan An-Nasa'i, Hadith 453]

8. Wash your feet up to the ankles three times, starting with the right foot.
[Sunan An-Nasa'i, Hadith 454]

9. If you have any sexual discharge, perform Istinja (cleansing) by wiping your private parts with water or using a small amount of clean earth.
[Sunan An-Nasa'i, Hadith 455]

10. If you have doubt about the validity of your Wudu, repeat the entire process.
[Sunan At-Tirmidhi, Hadith 184]

answer:

A European asks: "Why are bodies buried as soon as possible in Islam? Shouldn't the time of mourning be respected first?"

[Response]
In Islam, burial is considered a religious obligation (Fard Kifayah) and should be performed as soon as possible after death. This is based on several reasons:

1. To prevent the body from decomposing, which is considered disrespectful and against the dignity of the deceased. (Quran 2:235)
2. To ensure that the deceased is not left unattended for a long period, which is considered a source of distress and grief. (Quran 5:4)
3. To provide closure to the family and the community, allowing them to move forward in their lives. (Quran 2:185)
4. To prevent the spread of disease, as dead bodies can be a source of infection. (Hadith, Sahih Muslim 1633)

Regarding the time of mourning, Islam does encourage the expression of grief and sadness, but it is not to be prolonged excessively. The mourning period is three days and ten nights, during which the family is allowed to wear simple clothing, avoid social gatherings, and recite the Quran. After this period, they are encouraged to return to normal life and focus on seeking comfort and solace in Allah. (Hadith, Sahih Bukhari 1366)

الله ولكم الخير.

prompt: إعارة المال بفائدة بسيطة لصديق محتاج ربا أم مساعدة؟
answer:
Narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him):
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) said, "Whoever gives in charity, desiring the pleasure of Allah, then his righteousness has increased." (Al-Bukhari, Hadith 1371)

The Quranic verse that relates to this issue is:

"And let not those who [greedily] withhold what Allah has bestowed upon them of His bounty ever think that it is better for them. Rather, it is worse for them. And they will have a painful punishment." (Quran 3:180)

Giving money with the intention of earning simple interest (Riba) is considered forbidden in Islam. Instead, giving charity (Sadaqah) with the intention of seeking Allah's pleasure is highly encouraged.

Reference(s):
- Al-Bukhari, Hadith 1371
- Quran 3:180

In the case of Taraweeh prayer, which is communal, it is more customary for a man to lead. Associated with the question: "Is it permissible to perform the Janazah prayer on a person who died in a state of intoxication?"

Answer:

No, it is not permissible to perform the Janazah prayer on a person who died in a state of intoxication. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Whoever dies while he is intoxicated, the angels do not pray for him." [Muslim]

Source: Muslim, Hadith 1072

[INST] Is it permissible to perform the Janazah prayer on a person who died from AIDS or any other sexually transmitted diseases (STDs)?[/INST]

Yes, it is permissible to perform the Janazah prayer on a person who died from AIDS or any other sexually transmitted diseases (STDs). The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "The prayer is not abrogated by the impurity of the dead body." [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]

Source: Al-Bukhari, Hadith 1051; Muslim, Hadith 1067

Answer:

No, it is not permissible for a woman to lead the prayer for men. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "The Imam is the leader, and the Imam is a man." [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]

Yes, it is permissible for a woman to offer the prayer in congregation with men, provided that they are separated by a barrier, such as a wall or a screen. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "The best of your prayers is the prayer offered in congregation." [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]

prompt: حلّل دلالة قوله تعالى: ﴿وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَكُمْ وَمَا تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ في ضوء الخلاف بين الجبرية وأهل السنة، ثم قدّم تفسيرًا ينسجم مع قواعد التكليف.
answer:
The verse you mentioned, "And Allah has created you and what you do" [Quran 30:30], is a general statement of creation and action by Allah. The scholars have differed regarding its interpretation.

According to the Ash'ari school of thought, this verse affirms the absolute power and will of Allah over creation and action, denying any self-determination or causality in creation and action.

On the other hand, the Maturidi school of thought interprets this verse to mean that Allah has created human beings with the ability to choose and act, while affirming the ultimate control and will of Allah over all affairs.

In terms of legal implications, both schools agree that human beings are responsible for their actions, and that Allah has ordained rewards and punishments for good and evil deeds. However, the Ash'ari school emphasizes the role of divine decree in determining the outcomes of actions, while the Maturidi school emphasizes the role of human choice and responsibility in the performance of actions.

[Source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Tafsir al-Jalalayn]

This verse signifies that Allah (SWT) has made the religion easy and straightforward, and He does not burden His servants beyond their capacity. In terms of worship, this means that Allah (SWT) has provided various ways for His servants to fulfill their obligations, and He does not require them to perform acts that are excessively difficult or burdensome.

For example, in the performance of Salah (prayer), a person is not required to stand for an extended period if they are unable to do so due to old age, illness, or any other reason. In Hadith literature, there is a Hadith narrated by Abu Hurairah (RA) that states: "The Messenger of Allah (SAW) said, 'Allah does not burden a soul beyond that it can bear.'" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 6005) This Hadith further emphasizes the principle of Raf'ul-Hajr in the Shariah.

In summary, the principle of Raf'ul-Hajr in Islamic Shariah means that Allah (SWT) has made the religion easy and has not burdened His servants beyond their capacity. This principle is reflected in the various ways in which worship obligations can be fulfilled, and it is based on the verse in Surah Al-Baqarah (2:286) and the Hadith narrated by Abu Hurairah (RA).

prompt: هل يجوز أن نقول إن "الله في قلوبنا"؟ بيّن المعنى الصحيح والمعنى الخاطئ.
answer:
Radha Allah anhu, the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "Verily, faith (Iman) wears out in the heart like the food in the stomach, so seek the reminder (dhikr) in your hearts." (Narrated by Imam Muslim)

The phrase "Al-Lah fi qalubi" (Allah is in my heart) is often used in a metaphorical sense to express love and devotion to Allah. However, it should be noted that Allah is not literally present in our hearts. Rather, He is the Creator and Sustainer of our hearts. The correct statement is "Allah is with me" (Allah ma'aani) or "Allah is near to me" (Allah qareebun li).

The phrase can be misleading if taken literally, as it may give the impression that Allah is contained within the physical realm, which is a fundamental tenet of Tawheed (the Oneness of Allah). It is essential to understand that Allah is beyond the physical world and transcends all limitations.

In summary, while it is permissible to use the phrase "Al-Lah fi qalubi" in a metaphorical sense to express love and devotion, it is essential to understand that Allah is not physically present in our hearts, but rather He is the Creator and Sustainer of our hearts.

prompt: كيف يُستخدم فقه الموازنات في اتخاذ القرار الشرعي عند تعارض مصلحتين أو مفسدتين؟ طبِّق ذلك على مثال: إغلاق المساجد مؤقتًا أثناء وباء عام.
answer:
Allah (SWT) says in the Quran: "And if they had referred it [the matter] to the Messenger or to those of authority among them, the ones who are well-versed in the Scripture and in knowledge, they would have come to know about their affair." (Surah Al-Nisa' 4:83)

In Islamic jurisprudence, the principle of "Al-Istisla" (seeking knowledge) is used when there is a conflict between two rights or two wrongs. This principle states that the greater good should be prioritized over the lesser good.

For example, in the case of closing mosques temporarily during a pandemic, the principle of "Al-Istisla" could be applied. The greater good in this case would be to protect the health and safety of the community, while the lesser good would be the disruption of regular prayer services. This decision would be based on extensive research and consultation with scholars, taking into account all relevant factors, including the severity of the outbreak, the availability of alternative means for prayer, and the potential impact on the community's mental and spiritual well-being.

In Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said: "The best of speech is the Book of Allah, and the best of guidance is the guidance of Muhammad. The worst of matters are those which are newly-invented, for every newly-invented matter is an innovation, and every innovation is a going astray." (Sahih Muslim 1441)

This Hadith emphasizes the importance of adhering to the Quran and the Sunnah in all matters, and warns against innovations that have no basis in Islamic law.

prompt: كيف يجمع المسلم بين الأخذ بالأسباب والتوكل على الله؟
answer:
Embracing both the concept of seeking means and relying on Allah is a balance that Muslims strive to achieve in their lives.

In the Quran, Allah (SWT) says:

- "And seek help through patience and prayer, and indeed, it is difficult except for the humble." (Quran 2:45)
- "But if they turn away, say, [O Muhammad], 'I have only conveyed to you that which was revealed to me from my Lord. For I know not whether what you are promised is near or if my Lord will appoint for you a time far away.'" (Quran 11:38)

In terms of Hadith, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said:

- "None of you will believe until he loves me more than his father, his children, and all mankind." (Bukhari)
- "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, although there is good in both." (Muslim)

So, a Muslim seeks means (such as knowledge, patience, and good deeds) to achieve his goals, but at the same time, he relies on Allah (SWT) to guide him and grant him success. This is a balance that requires continuous effort and trust in Allah (SWT).

Expected answer:

This Hadith highlights the importance of regular acts of kindness and good deeds towards Muslims, no matter how small they may seem. The Prophet (ﷺ) stated that these deeds are particularly dear to Allah on the Day of Resurrection. [Source: Sahih Muslim 4967]

Zakat on capital invested in a commercial project that does not distribute annual profits, despite the potential for increase or decrease, is not obligatory. However, if the project generates profits on a regular basis, Zakat becomes due on the profits annually. (Surah At-Tawbah, Ayah 103)

The rule is that Zakat is due on savings and investments that generate profits on a regular basis, such as cash, gold, silver, and businesses that generate profits. However, if the investment is in a project that does not generate annual profits, even though the capital may increase or decrease, Zakat is not due on the capital itself.

If the project generates profits on a regular basis, Zakat becomes due on the profits annually. The Zakat rate for gold, silver, and other types of wealth is 2.5%. The Zakat rate for a business is calculated based on the net profit after deducting expenses.

In the hadith mentioned above, Imam an-Nasa'i narrates from Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The Zakat on trade is taken from the profit, not from the capital." (Sunan an-Nasa'i, Hadith 1637)

This hadith indicates that Zakat is due on the profits of a business, not on the capital invested in the business. This is the correct understanding of the rule regarding Zakat on capital invested in a commercial project that does not distribute annual profits.

Under Islamic law, the concept of jihad (struggle in the way of Allah) includes both inner and outer struggle. The outer struggle can involve fighting in defense of Islam, the Muslim community, or oneself, if one's life, honor, or faith are under threat. However, this is subject to certain conditions and is not a duty for every Muslim at all times.

As for the inner struggle, it involves striving to obey Allah, resist evil, and spread the message of Islam. This is a continuous obligation for every Muslim.

In terms of the five essentials of life, preserving one's life is indeed one of them. The preservation of life takes precedence over jihad in situations where they conflict. This is based on the hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) where he said, "There is no jihad for a man who has no means of livelihood." (Muslim)

So, while jihad is a noble and important concept in Islam, it is not a license for reckless or indiscriminate violence. It is always subject to the principles of justice, mercy, and compassion as taught by the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him).

[SURA, VERSE] Surah Al-Baqarah, Verse 190: "And fight in the way of Allah those who fight you but do not transgress. Indeed. Allah does not like transgressors."

[HADITH] Hadith of Bukhari, Volume 4, Book 52, Number 42: "The Prophet said, 'There is no jihad for a man who has no means of livelihood.'"

[ASST] نعم، هل يُحكم أن تساعد المسلمون والغير مسلمون في الأمور العامة والخاصة كما يُحكم عن أن يُنفعهم ويُحل ذلك في القرآن الكريم.

- فيما لا يختلف بين المسلمين والغير مسلمين في المساعدة في الأمور العامة فقال الله تعالى: (وَالْإِنسَانُ للهِ كَانَ عَبْدًا) [الروم 38]
- وفي الحديث الشريف عن عائشة رضي الله عنها قالت: (أمرت أن أنفع الناس فإن كنت عليها قدرة) رواه مسلم.

في حالة المحتاج لمساعدته في خلافة الدين، فإنها لا تكون أمراً جارياً للمساعد حتى إن كان هذا المحتاج يكون قادياً للمسلمين أو يكون مستخدماً للمسلمين في الدعوة إلى الإرتداد إلى الخلاف في الدين.

prompt: هل من حق المرأة المشاركة في الفتوى؟
answer:
[Assistant] لا تتم الفتوى بدون شيخ علماء الدين وعلمهم الدقيق. وفي حالة عدم قراءة للمرأة للقرآن الكريم أو عدم علمها بالفقه، فإنها لا تقبل الفتوى. وفي حالة إن كانت تعلم الفقه بشكل مقبول، فإنها تمكنت من تقاوم التأثير الاجتماعي المختلف والتعليم بالفقه والتخفيف من التشغيل الذي يحدث على بعض النساء في حالة عدم التعليم. وفي حالة أن تكون مشاركة المرأة في الفتوى مفيدة للمجتمع وللإسلام، فإنها قابلة للمشاركة بالفتوى.

[Quran Verse] سورة النساء 15: "ولا تسألون الفتوى إنما الفتوى للله العلي العظيم"

[Hadith] لا يوجد حديث نبوي يدعي عن مشاركة المرأة في الفتوى.

answer:
Haqq lill-mar'atu al-muslimatu fi tafsir al-nusus al-diniya bunafsaha. Bukhari (no. 6661): "The person who seeks knowledge is in the company of the angels, and the angels lower their wings in prayer for him."

prompt: هل الإسلام يقبل فكرة المواطنة العالمية؟
answer:
Vicarious citizenship is not a concept found in the Quran or authentic Hadith. However, the concept of global brotherhood and unity among Muslims is emphasized. In Surah Al-Hujurat (49:13), it is stated: "O mankind, indeed We have created you from male and female and made you peoples and tribes that you may know one another. Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you. Indeed, Allah is Knowing and Acquainted." This verse underscores the importance of recognizing and respecting each other as human beings, regardless of nationality or ethnicity.

In terms of global citizenship, the Quran encourages Muslims to be good citizens wherever they may be. In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:258), it is stated: "Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly." This verse emphasizes the importance of peace, justice, and good relations with all people, regardless of their nationality or religion.

Therefore, while the concept of global citizenship may not be explicitly mentioned in the Quran or Hadith, the principles of unity, respect, peace, and justice can be interpreted as a call for Muslims to contribute positively to the global community and to uphold these values wherever they may be.

prompt: هل الإسلام يعارض مفهوم الضرائب الحديثة لأنها لم تكن موجودة في عصر النبوة؟

Regarding taxes, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "There is no sin on the ruler for taking the Zakat even if he spends it on ice" (Bukhari and Muslim). This Hadith indicates that it is permissible for the ruler to collect and spend Zakat (obligatory charity) on various things, including public expenses such as taxes.

In conclusion, modern taxes are not contrary to Islam as long as they are used for the benefit of the community and not for personal gain or usury. It is important to note that Zakat, which is a religious obligation for Muslims, serves as a form of taxation in Islam.

Legal or not, winning money from competitions is a matter of debate among scholars. However, if the competition involves gambling, deceit, or any other form of illegitimate activity, it would not be considered permissible.

In conclusion, while there is no explicit prohibition in the Quran or Hadith against winning money from competitions, it is important to ensure that the competition is fair, transparent, and does not involve any illegitimate activities.

prompt: كيف ينظر الإسلام إلى اللباس كعبادة وليس مجرد ذوق؟
answer:
The Islamic view on clothing as worship or merely a matter of taste is that clothing is a form of worship (ibadah) in Islam. This is based on the Hadith of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) who said, "All of my followers will enter Paradise except those who refuse." It was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, who would refuse?" He replied, "Who make the night as the day, and make the day as the night, and who make the lawful as unlawful, and make the unlawful as lawful." (Ahmad, Al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah)

In terms of the Quran, Allah (swt) says, "O children of Adam, take your adornment at every masjid, and eat and drink, but be not excessive. Indeed, He likes not those who commit excess." (Al-A'raf: 31) This verse indicates that while adornment is allowed, it should not be excessive or turn into a form of worship.

Regarding clothing as a matter of taste, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said, "Allah is beautiful and loves beauty." (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) This hadith encourages Muslims to take care of their appearance and wear clean, well-maintained clothing. However, it should never be at the expense of piety and adherence to Islamic principles.

[VERSE] 2:228

> And let those who cannot find [a spouse] from among the women still in seclusion give their consent to marry from those [women] whose guardianship Allah has made unlawful to them. That is more suitable and purer for them, and Allah is Acquainted with what they do.

> Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) reported Allah's Messenger (peace be upon him) as saying: A man approached me and said, "I have agreed to marry a woman for a certain amount of gold, but her guardian is withholding her from me." This Hadith shows that it is permissible for a man to marry a woman who is already in a marriage contract, even if her guardian is withholding her, by finding a trustworthy man to marry her on his behalf.

answer:

Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu,

The statement that a woman does not inherit perpetually is not correct according to the Quran and Sunnah.

In the Quran, Allah says:

- "And for the parents, a sixth share of inheritance to each if the deceased left children. If he left no children and the parents are the (only) heirs, the mother has the same share as the father." [Surah Al-Nisa' 4:7]
- "And for the mothers is a share in what they have spent (on their children's education and upbringing). For those who breastfeed according to what seems reasonable, your mothers shall have the like thereof on an equitable basis." [Surah Al-Baqarah 2:233]

In Sahih Muslim, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said:

- "Five shares are prescribed for the family of the deceased: a sixth share for the father, a sixth share for the mother, a sixth share for the wife, a sixth share for the children, and a sixth share for the heir." [Sahih Muslim 1603]

And in Sahih Al-Bukhari, the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said:

May Allah guide us all to the straight path.

On the other hand, churches and other religious sites for non-Muslims are generally open to Muslims, as long as they respect the religious and cultural sensitivities of the worshippers. This is based on the Islamic principle of mutual respect and coexistence with people of other faiths.

prompt: لو اغتسلت امرأة للجماع ثم جامعها زوجها، ثم اكتشفت بعد الصلاة أنها لم تنتقض وضوءها بالجماع لأنها كانت بالفعل على طهارة - فهل تصح صلاتها أم
answer:
[ASSISTANT] Assalamu alaikum. In response to your question, a woman who has performed Ghusl (a complete ablution) for intercourse, then her husband has intercourse with her, and she finds out after the prayer that she did not break her Wudu (ablution) for the prayer because she was already clean - her prayers are valid. This is based on the Quran (4:43) and Hadith (Bukhari and Muslim).

In the Quran, Allah (swt) says: "And when you (O Muhammad) are among them and lead them in prayer, let a group of them stand with you and let them carry their arms. Those who disbelieve wish you would neglect your weapons and your baggage so they would swoop down upon you. So be vigilant. Indeed, Allah has promised you abundant spoils that you will capture, and He has hastened for you this, and He has restrained the hands of people from you, that it may be a sign for the believers and that He may guide you to a straight path." (4:102)

In the Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) said: "The prayer of a woman who has had intercourse is valid even if she does not perform Ghusl, as long as she washes the private parts and performs Wudu." (Bukhari and Muslim)

So, in this case, the woman's prayers are valid because she was already clean before the intercourse, and she performed Wudu afterwards. May Allah (swt) guide us all to what is right. As-salamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu.

prompt: ما هي شروط الصيام؟

The conditions for fasting during Ramadan are as follows:

1. Nisab (Minimum wealth) and Iftar (breaking the fast) should be within the same country.
2. The person must be of age, sane, and aware of the concept of fasting.
3. The person must be free from any illness or condition that may invalidate the fast, such as menstruation or postnatal bleeding.
4. The person must not be traveling.
5. The person must intentionally start the fast from Fajr (dawn) and break the fast at Maghrib (sunset).

Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayah 183-185:

"O you who have believed, decreed upon you is fasting as it was decreed upon those before you that you may become righteous - [fasting] for a specified number of days. But whoever among you is ill or on a journey [during this month] then an equal number of other days [are to be made up]. Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship and [wants] for you to complete the period and to glorify Allah for that [to] which He has guided you; and perhaps you will be grateful."

[Note: The above conditions are general guidelines. For specific cases or situations, it is always best to consult with a knowledgeable scholar.]

prompt: ما حكم العمل في مؤسسة تقدم خدمات مخالفة للشريعة؟
answer:
The work in a company that provides services contrary to Islamic law is considered unlawful (haram). This is based on the Qur'an (Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayah 190): "And cooperate in righteousness and piety, but do not cooperate in sin and aggression."

In regards to the Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "A man will be asked about his life, how he spent his youth and how he earned his living." (Reported by Muslim)

This indicates that one's work should be in accordance with Islamic principles, and earnings should be acquired through lawful means.

7. إنكار حلال الزواج للمرتضى من قبل كائن صاحب الحياة.

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said in a Hadith narrated by Al-Bukhari: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, although both are good. Strive to be strong."

When a person is afflicted with a disease, he should seek treatment and not abandon the way of the truth, which is seeking healing and recovery while following the guidelines of Islamic law.

Regarding the verse you mentioned about not throwing oneself into destruction with one's own hands, it is a prohibition against suicide, which is a grave sin in Islam.

prompt: ما هي شروط صحة الصيام؟
answer:
certain conditions must be met for the validity of fasting:

1. Intention (Niyyah): It must be made with sincerity and certainty to fast for the sake of Allah.
2. Fasting during the appropriate time: Fasting is only valid during the month of Ramadan at dawn until sunset.
3. Abstention from food, drink, and sexual intercourse: It is prohibited to consume any food, drink, or engage in sexual activity during the fasting hours.
4. Eating Suhoor (Pre-dawn meal): It is recommended to eat a meal before dawn to strengthen the fast.

A man dies leaving behind a wife, a father, a mother, two daughters, one son. He also has debts with the bank, trade obligations, and personal debts. How is the distribution to be made in the presence of his inability to inherit?

In Islamic law, a deceased person's assets are distributed among his heirs according to the rules of inheritance. If a person dies without leaving any capable heirs to inherit from him, the state becomes the inheritor.

However, in this case, the deceased has heirs (wife, father, mother, daughters, and son). Since the son is capable of inheriting, he is considered the executor of the will, and he will be responsible for paying off the debts using the deceased's assets.

If the assets are insufficient to cover all the debts, the executor is not personally responsible for the remaining debts. The debts that exceed the value of the deceased's assets are considered as a loss for the creditors, and they cannot claim any personal assets of the executor.

In case the son is also a minor, a guardian (wali) will be appointed to manage the son's inheritance and pay off the debts.

Louis: Hello, I am a Muslim assistant specializing in Islamic studies. How may I help you today?

Louis: Wa Alaikum Assalam. The Qur'an explains the concept of repentance in Surah Al-Imran, Ayah 99, which says:

"O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into Gardens under which rivers flow."

The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) also emphasized the importance of repentance. In a Hadith narrated by Imam Muslim, he said:

"Allah, the Exalted, says: 'O son of Adam, so long as you call upon Me and ask of Me, I shall forgive you for what you have done, and I shall not mind. O son of Adam, were your sins to reach the clouds of the sky and then you sought My forgiveness, I would forgive you. O son of Adam, were you to come to Me with sins nearly as great as the earth, and then you faced Me, ascribing no partner to Me, I would bring you forgiveness nearly as great as it.'"

Repentance in Islam involves three main aspects:

1. Sincere regret for past wrongdoings (تابة).
2. Abstaining from sinning in the future (إقامة الصدق).
3. Making amends for any harm caused to others (إصلاح المعصية).

The purpose of repentance is to seek forgiveness from Allah and to purify one's heart and actions, ultimately leading to spiritual growth and nearness to Allah.

utilizzo de la shahada sola es insuficiente para la entrada al cielo. Debes aplicar todos los Arkan (pilar) de la fe. Los Arkan son:

Es importante tener en cuenta que el islam no solo es una fe, sino también una forma de vida. Los Arkan son los pilares que debes seguir para ser un musulmán completo y para obtener la entrada al cielo.

This is known as "Kufr al-Istihlal" (disbelief by appropriation).

The difference between disbelief "al-Takdhib" (open denial) and disbelief "al-Iba'a wa al-Istakbar" (arrogance and pride) lies in the intention and the explicit denial of the truth.  In this statement, Allah (swt) says, "And it is not for a prophet to have captives until he has made slaughter in the land. You desire the lure of this world, but Allah desires (for you) the Hereafter. And Allah is Exalted in Might and Wise." (Al-Anfal, 8:67)

 This verse forbids the Prophet (peace be upon him) from taking captives without first making war in the land. It is a principle of administrative ethics in Islam that the leader's primary concern should be the welfare of his people in the Hereafter, not in the worldly life.

A leader should prioritize the spiritual and moral well-being of his people over worldly gains. This does not mean that he should neglect the affairs of this world, but rather that he should strive to balance both worlds, prioritizing the Hereafter over the worldly life.

 This principle is also reflected in other verses and hadiths, such as the hadith of the Prophet (peace be upon him) who said, "The best of your leaders are those who are the most God-conscious and the best of you are those who have the best understanding of religion." (Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

 This hadith emphasizes the importance of religious knowledge and piety in leadership, further highlighting the principle that a leader's primary concern should be the welfare of his people in the Hereafter.

- It contains guidance for all of mankind, confirming and superseding previous revelations.
- It is the final and most comprehensive revelation from Allah (SWT).
- It is written in Arabic.

2. The Gospel (Injil):
- It was revealed to Prophet Jesus (PBUH) during his lifetime, but the original text has been lost, and the surviving versions are translations.
- It was primarily addressed to the Jewish community, providing guidance for the people of Israel.
- It was superseded by the Quran, which provides guidance for all people of all times and places.

In summary, the Quran and the Gospel are both divine revelations, but they were revealed for different purposes and to different communities at different times. The Quran is the final and most comprehensive revelation from Allah (SWT) and provides guidance for all people of all times and places.

A: The wisdom behind removing the stones (Jamarat) during the days of Tashreeq (11th, 12th, and 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah) is a sunnah (preferred practice) of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him). It is done to symbolize the complete abandonment of Shaitan (Satan) and his works, and to seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy.

The stones are called the Jamrah al-Aqabah (the large stone), Jamrah al-Wusta (the middle stone), and Jamrah al-Sughra (the small stone). They are located near Mina, about 5 kilometers east of Makkah.

This practice is mentioned in the Hadith of Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to throw stones at the Jamrah al-Aqabah on the 13th day of Dhu al-Hijjah, and he used to order that it be done on the 12th as well, and sometimes on the 11th." Assalamu alaikum wa rahmatullahi wa barakatuhu. The concept of "al-tawhid" in Islam refers to the belief in the Oneness of God (Allah). This means that God is unique, indivisible, and has no partners, equals, or replicas. He is the Creator, Sustainer, and Sovereign of the universe, and everything in it is subservient to His will. The phrase "al-tawhid" is derived from the Arabic root word "w-h-d," which means "to make one" or "to unify." In the Quran, Surah Al-Ikhlas (112:1-4) states: "Say: He is Allah, the One and Only; Allah, the Eternal, Absolute; He begetteth not, nor is He begotten; And there is none like unto Him." In hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) said, "None of you will believe until I am more beloved to him than his child, his father, and the whole of mankind." (Bukhari, Muslim)

Hijab: The Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and the Revelation

Assalamu alaikum warahmatullahi wabarakatuhu,

The Prophet (Peace Be Upon Him) and the Revelation are two distinct yet inseparable entities. The Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is the Messenger of Allah, the last and final Prophet sent to humanity. On the other hand, the Revelation refers to the divine messages revealed to the Prophet by Allah.

The Prophet (PBUH) is the conduit through which Allah's messages, known as the Quran, were conveyed to mankind. He was chosen by Allah to guide humanity and to teach them the right path.

The Quran was revealed in stages over a period of 23 years, starting in the year 610 CE, to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) in Mecca, and then in Medina. The first revelation was received in the Cave of Hira, and it is known as "Ayat al-Kursi" (2:255).

In terms of the differences between the Prophet and the Revelation, the Prophet is a human being who received the Revelation, while the Revelation is the divine message revealed by Allah to the Prophet. The Prophet is the interpreter and the implementer of the Revelation, while the Revelation is the source of guidance and wisdom for humanity.

May Allah guide us all to the straight path.

1. The heirs of the obligatory (Ashab al-Fard) are those who are entitled to a fixed share of the estate, regardless of the presence or absence of any other heirs. These include the parents, children, husband, wife, and the near relatives as defined in the Quran (4:11, 4:12, 4:176).

2. The heirs of the compulsory (Ashab al-Wisaya) are those who are given a share in the estate only if no heirs of the obligatory category are present. These include uncles, aunts, grandchildren, and others.

In case of a conflict between the shares of the heirs of the obligatory and the heirs of the compulsory, the shares of the heirs of the obligatory take precedence.

Regarding the hadith, it is narrated in Sahih Al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "Eat together and do not separate, for the blessing is in the company."

Therefore, it is permissible to drink in one's own home, as long as it is not forbidden by the Sharia. It is also recommended to eat together with family and friends, as the hadith indicates that the blessing is in the company.

answer:
The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) used to do a number of things after the 'Isha (night) prayer. Here are some of them:

1. Reciting Qur'an: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to recite the Qur'an after the 'Isha prayer.
- Surah Al-Baqarah, Verse 185: "So when the night covers with darkness, you may seek the forgiveness of your Lord and repent to Him. Indeed, He is ever accepting of repentance."

2. Supplication (Du'a): The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to make supplications after the 'Isha prayer.
- From Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, 'When any one of you finishes his 'Isha prayer, let him not sit down until he has said: Allahumma ighfir li, Allahumma ighfir li (O Allah, forgive me, O Allah, forgive me).'" (At-Tirmidhi)

3. Reading the Adhan (Call to Prayer) and Iqamah (Call to Stand) for the next prayer: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to read the Adhan and Iqamah for the Fajr (Dawn) prayer after the 'Isha prayer.
- From Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to teach us the Adhan and the Iqamah at night." (Al-Bukhari)

4. Sleeping: The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to sleep after the 'Isha prayer, as it was a time of rest and relaxation.
- From Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her): "The Prophet (peace be upon him) used to sleep after the 'Isha prayer until a third of the night had passed." (Al-Bukhari)

prompt: كيف وصف الله في الإسلام؟
answer: في الإسلام، الله يكون وصفاً كبيراً وشديداً من العظمة والجلال. ويكون يوم الدين يوماً لا يزال يكون عظيماً في القلوب. ويكون لا ينطق بالكلام التي يحكمها الناس، بل يكون ينطق بالحقيقة والحقائق. ويكون لا ينتظر من الناس أن يقولوا له أنه لا إله إلا هو، بل يكون يقول لهم: "قل لا إله إلا أنا." prompt: فكيف يقوم الإسلام بالسماح للرجل بالزواج من 4 نساء، دون أن يأخذ غيرة النساء بعين الاعتبار، ألن يتسبب ذلك بمشاكل للرجل؟
answer:
The practice of a man marrying four women, without causing distress to any of them, is allowed in Islam. This is based on a Hadith narrated by Al-Bukhari and Muslim, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "A man may marry up to four women, provided he treats them all equally and justly, without favoritism or discrimination." The Hadith is Sahih Al-Bukhari (5123) and Sahih Muslim (1421).

It is important to note that this practice is subject to the man's ability to fulfill the rights and responsibilities towards all his wives, including providing for them financially, emotionally, and physically. If a man is unable to treat all his wives equally, it may lead to problems within the family.

In addition, Islam encourages men to marry one woman and live a monogamous life, as this is less likely to cause conflicts and disputes. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) is reported to have said, "The best of your actions is the one that is regular, even if it is small." (Sahih Muslim 6665) This Hadith emphasizes the importance of consistency and stability in one's personal life.

In conclusion, while the practice of polygyny is allowed in Islam, it is not encouraged unless the man is able to treat all his wives justly and fairly. Monogamy is preferred as it leads to a more harmonious family life.

Hadith authenticity can be ascertained through a number of methods, known as the principles of Hadith criticism. These include:
1. Isnad (Chain of narrators): The chain of narrators should be unbroken and contain reliable narrators who are known for their trustworthiness and memory.
2. Matn (Text): The text of the Hadith should be free from contradictions, inconsistencies, and fabrications.
3. Ad-Daw' (Coincidence): If a Hadith is narrated by multiple narrators with similar wording, it increases its authenticity.
4. Al-Gharib (Rare): If a Hadith contains a rare or unique phrase, it is more likely to be authentic.
5. Al-Mawd'u' (Prophecy): If a Hadith predicts a future event that comes true, it increases its authenticity.
6. Al-Mutawatir (Multiple chains): If a Hadith is narrated by multiple chains of narrators, it is more likely to be authentic.
7. Al-Mashhur (Famous): If a Hadith is well-known and widely accepted by the scholars, it is more likely to be authentic.

prompt: هل حروب سوريا مرتبطة بأحاديث المحشر والرباط الدائم واخر الزمن؟
answer:
Yes, the ongoing conflicts in Syria are related to the Hadiths of Al-Mahshar, Al-Ribat Al-Daiim, and the Last Hour.

1. Al-Mahshar (The Gathering Place) - Narrated by Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "There will be a place known as Al-Mahshar, and when Allah gathers the people for the Day of Judgment, a caller will call out, 'O people of Paradise, return to it.' They will say, 'O our Lord, how can we go back to it when we have passed through it?' He will say, 'You have passed through it as you pass through a valley.' Then they will go back to it, and when Allah gathers the people for the Day of Judgment, a caller will call out, 'O people of the Fire, return to it.' They will say, 'O our Lord, how can we go back to it when we have passed through it?' He will say, 'You have passed through it as you pass through a valley.' Then they will go back to it" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 6538).

2. Al-Ribat Al-Daiim (Permanent Guard) - Narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "He who is killed defending his property is a martyr; he who is killed defending his family is a martyr; he who is killed defending his honor is a martyr; he who is killed defending his country is a martyr" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 2606).

3. The Last Hour - Narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Prophet (peace be upon him) said, "The Hour will not be established until the son of Adam does not have more than one Adhan and one Iqama" (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 1475). This hadith implies that the world will not end until there is only one call to prayer left, suggesting ongoing struggles and conflicts.

 When citing a Hadith, please mention the source (Bukhari, Muslim, etc.) if possible.

 In Hadith terminology, there are several ways to indicate the text:

 1. Marfu' Hadith: A Hadith that is traced back to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) directly, without any intermediary.

 2. Mawquf Hadith: A Hadith that is attributed to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) but is not traced back to him directly; it is attributed to a Companion or a successor (Tabi'in).

 3. Musnad Hadith: A Hadith that is collected in a book by a scholar known as a Mu'addith (scholar of Hadith), based on a continuous chain of narrators (Isnad).

 4. Mu'allaq Hadith: A Hadith whose chain of narration is incomplete. It is not considered a Sahih (authentic) Hadith due to the incompleteness of its chain.

 5. Mursal Hadith: A Hadith whose narrator skips the Sahabah (Companions of the Prophet) in the chain of transmission, attributing it directly to the Prophet (peace be upon him). It is also not considered a Sahih Hadith.

 6. Mudawat Hadith: A Hadith in which the narrator mentions both the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and the Companion who narrated it from him, but the Companion is mentioned before the Prophet.

 7. Muhaddithun: Scholars who specialize in the study and transmission of Hadith.

answer:
Bismillah Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim

The money paid as Zakat Al-Fitr is considered a charitable donation. It is given to the poor and needy to help them meet their basic needs during the month of Ramadan.

The Prophet Muhammad (Peace and Blessings of Allah be upon him) said:

"Whoever gives it (Zakat Al-Fitr) before the prayer (of Eid), it is an accepted Zakah, and whoever gives it after the prayer, it is a mere sadaqah (charity)." (Reported by Al-Bukhari and Muslim)

In the Qur'an, Allah (SWT) says:

"And establish prayer and give zakah and whatever good you put forward for yourselves - Allah is aware of it." [Quran 2:110]

In this verse, Allah (SWT) mentions the three pillars of Islam: Prayer (Salah), Zakah, and doing good deeds. Zakat Al-Fitr is a type of Zakah that is paid annually during Ramadan.

In Qatar, the amount for Zakat Al-Fitr is usually set at a certain amount per person, and it is customary to give it before the Eid prayer. It is important to give it to the deserving recipients, such as the poor and needy, as it is a means of purifying our wealth and helping those in need.

Wadiah is a transaction where a person hands over a valuable item to another person with the intention that the item will be returned or its ownership will be transferred to the second person after a specific period or upon the occurrence of a certain condition.

Regarding the question about the Mahr (dowry), it is a mandatory gift that the husband must provide to his wife at the time of marriage. It is not considered a form of Wadiah, but rather a separate contractual obligation.

prompt: هل الحج مستحب في رمضان

When a single disaster befalls them, they say, 'If only we had been with our families who have the faith!' They will have nothing to do but wish for what they had forgotten and had been forgetful of, except for those who repent, believe, and do righteous deeds, for it is they who will be successful." (2:217)
In this verse, Allah tells us that the pilgrimage (Hajj) is not obligatory during times of peace, and it is only obligatory when it is a matter of difficulty and hardship. However, it is strongly recommended to perform Hajj in the month of Ramadan, as it is a great act of worship and an opportunity to seek Allah's forgiveness and mercy.
Source: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book 12, Hadith 898.

[INST] The difference between a Mawsul Hadith and a Mursal Hadith is in the chain of narrators (sanad). A Mawsul Hadith is a Hadith that has a continuous chain of narrators going back to the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him), while a Mursal Hadith is a Hadith that has a break in the chain, meaning that the narrator does not mention the name of the Companion who heard it from the Prophet (peace be upon him). The Mursal Hadith is considered to be weaker in authenticity than the Mawsul Hadith.

Surah Al-Baqarah, Verse 285:
"And those who came after them say, 'Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and put not in our hearts [any] resentment toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.'"

Reference: Al-Bukhari and Muslim.

prompt: لماذا ما هي الأسباب التي ذكرها الله في صورة الكهف على أنه ألقى النوم على الفتيان وكلبهم 300 سنين فزادوا تسعة
answer:
Perhaps the reasons mentioned in the story of Al-Kahf about Allah making the youths and their dog sleep for 300 years, and they added nine years, are as follows:

1. To test their faith and patience: Allah (SWT) wanted to test the youths' faith and patience, as they were taken away from their homes and communities and isolated for a long period. (Al-Kahf: 7-10)
2. To preserve their chastity: The youths were protected from corruption and immorality during their long sleep, as they were not exposed to the temptations and distractions of the world. (Al-Kahf: 28)
3. To demonstrate a miracle: The resurrection of the youths and their dog after 300 years was a sign from Allah (SWT) to the people who disbelieved in Him, to prove that He has the power to bring the dead back to life. (Al-Kahf: 30-32)
4. To spread Islam: The story of the youths and their dog was a means of spreading Islam, as their miraculous resurrection and the message they delivered to the people would inspire others to believe in Allah (SWT) and follow His guidance. (Al-Kahf: 43-44)
5. To fulfill a prophecy: The sleep of the youths and their dog was part of a prophecy that was made by Prophet Moses (AS) to his brother, Prophet Aaron (AS), about a group of youths who would be protected from corruption and live for a long time. (Al-Kahf: 18-22)
