prompt: حكم رخصة الصلاة للعروس في يوم زفافها
answer:
Twenty-four hours before the wedding day, it is permissible for the bride to perform her obligatory prayers in full, according to the hadith narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'If a man gets married, he should not pray the night prayer for twenty nights or perform the day prayer for twenty days.'" [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]

As for the bride, she is allowed to shorten her prayers during the wedding day due to the hardship it causes, as stated in the hadith narrated by Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'There is no hardship for a woman except in three things: menstruation, postnatal bleeding, and the day of her wedding.'" [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]

The bride can shorten her prayers by performing the two Rak'ahs of the noon, afternoon, sunset, and night prayers instead of the four Rak'ahs. She can also combine the morning and noon prayers if she wishes. However, she is not allowed to skip any of the five daily prayers, as they are obligatory.

The bride is also allowed to delegate her prayers to another woman during the wedding day, as stated in the hadith narrated by Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said, 'If any woman gets married, let her delegate her prayers to another woman during the three days of her wedding.'" [Al-Bukhari and Muslim]

It is also permissible for the bride to perform her prayers during the night of her wedding if she wishes, as stated in the hadith narrated by Ibn 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) used to pray during the night of his daughter's wedding." [Al-Bukhari]

prompt: ما الحكمة من القسم في سورة الشمس خاصة القسم بالنفس
answer:
Nafs: سورة النفس (12:1-11)

 The Verse of the Soul (Al-Nafs):

 In Surah Al-Nafs (The Soul), Allah says:

 "The soul and him who is self-conscious thereof will dispute with him about his departure (from this world): 'O soul, you have indeed corrupted yourself.'

 'Nay, (it was) our Lord! Indeed, he had exalted us (in position), and (given us) our due portion, and we have made abomination (of) what they have worshipped besides You.

 'If You had intended to try us, You could have tried us through what You have given us. Indeed, we would have been patient, and indeed, we would have turned back (to You) and indeed, we would have been obedient.

 'But when You took us and buried us by (the will of) a predetermined destiny, then You brought us forth (again) and gave us a shape (that is) how You willed. We would then have said, 'O our Lord, show us the good (reward) for what I did when I was patient, and for what I did when I was a believer.'

 'So We will surely record it in a book (of deeds). Then We will recount it for you with knowledge, and indeed, We will make it easy for you to understand.

 'So, exalted is Allah, the King, the Truth, and He does not take a son, and to Him belongs all that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth. And sufficient is Allah as a Disposer of affairs."

 The Verse of the Soul is a dialogue between the soul and Allah, in which the soul argues that it has obeyed Allah and been patient, and therefore should be rewarded for its good deeds. Allah responds by promising to record the soul's deeds in a book and to make it easy for the soul to understand its reward. The verse emphasizes Allah's greatness and power, and affirms that He does not take a son and that all things belong to Him.

وهكذا يجب أن نتخذ بالنواعي، ونعتمد على القرآن والسنة في الأمور الأسلمية.

prompt: ما هي خطوات العمرة؟
answer:
Al-'Umrah and Hajj are the fifth and the final pillars of Islam, respectively. The steps for performing 'Umrah are as follows:

1. Ihram: Put on the Ihram, which is a special garment for pilgrims.
2. Tawaf: Perform Tawaf Al-Qudum, which is the circumambulation of the Ka'bah seven times.
3. Sa'i: Perform Sa'i, which is the running or walking between Safa and Marwah seven times.
4. Shaving or Cutting Hair: For men, shave their head or cut a small amount of hair. For women, they only need to perform Tahalul, which is the removal of a small amount of hair from the head.
5. Tawaf Al-Wadaa': Perform Tawaf Al-Wadaa', which is the final circumambulation of the Ka'bah.

The steps for Hajj are similar to 'Umrah, but with additional rituals:

1. Ihram: Put on the Ihram.
2. Tawaf Al-Qudum: Perform Tawaf Al-Qudum.
3. Sa'i: Perform Sa'i.
4. Arafat: Spend the day at Mount Arafat.
5. Muzdalifah: Stay at Muzdalifah after sunset and perform Maghrib and 'Isha prayers.
6. Mina: Move to Mina and perform the stoning of the Jamrat Al-Aqabah.
7. Sacrifice: Perform the sacrifice (Udhiyah) of a sheep, camel, cow, or goat.
8. Tawaf Al-Ifadah: Perform Tawaf Al-Ifadah.
9. Farewell Tawaf: Perform Tawaf Al-Wadaa'.

Answer:
When traveling, the prayer times are shortened. The prayer of Zuhr (noon prayer) is shortened to two Rak'ahs, and the prayer of Asr (afternoon prayer) can be prayed with two Rak'ahs.

Quranic reference: Surah Al-Baqarah, Verse 185: "So when you travel throughout the land, there is no blame upon you for shortening the prayer, [especially] if you fear that those who disbelieve will cause you harm. Indeed, the disbelievers are ever unlawful for you."

Hadith reference: Sahih al-Bukhari, Book 1, Hadith 3: "Narrated 'Umar bin Al-Khattab: Allah's Apostle said, 'The prayer (performed) in a journey is shortened.' I asked, 'O Allah's Apostle! What about the night prayer?' He replied, 'It is as it was (i.e., the whole night).' I asked, 'What about the prayer of Fajr (morning)?' He replied, 'It is (performed) as it was.' I asked, 'What about the prayer of 'Isha'?' He replied, 'It is (performed) as it was.' I asked, 'What about the prayer of Zuhr (noon)?' He replied, 'It is two Rak'ahs,' I asked, 'What about the prayer of Asr (afternoon)?' He replied, 'It is two Rak'ahs.'"

prompt: ارني الاحاديث التي تذكر اعطاء الله ما سئل
answer:
Any time the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) was asked about a matter, he would refer back to the Qur'an and the Sunnah (his sayings, actions, and approval).

1. The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked, "O Messenger of Allah, what is the best deed?" He replied, "Believing in Allah and His Messenger." (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 1)

2. The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked, "Which deed is loved most by Allah?" He replied, "When a person revives an abandoned good practice." (Sahih Muslim, Hadith 122)

3. The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked, "Which charity is the best?" He replied, "Giving water to drink." (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 5037)

4. The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked, "What is the best form of prayer after the established prayer?" He replied, "To go to the market and trade, and give a portion of it in charity." (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 6981)

5. The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked, "What is the best kind of fasting after Ramadan?" He replied, "Fasting three days in a month." (Sahih Muslim, Hadith 1162)

6. The Prophet (peace be upon him) was asked, "What is the best form of jihad?" He replied, "A word of truth in the presence of a tyrant ruler." (Sahih Al-Bukhari, Hadith 42)

prompt: ماذا نقول يوم الجمعة عندما تصبح على احد
answer:
According to the Quran, when it becomes Friday, we say:

> سورة الجمعة, آية 9: وَقَالُوا يَا رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لَنَا إِن تَشَاءُ وَتَوَفَّنَا مَعَ الْإِيمَانِ

Translation: "Our Lord, forgive us our sins and remove from us our misdeeds, and make us die with the Islam as a group (submission to Allah alone)."

And in the Hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:

> حديث مسلم: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: لا تقولوا يوم الجمعة أحد الأيام أفضل منها، ولا تقولوا للصباح أفضل من الليل ولا تقولوا للليل أفضل من الصباح

Translation: "The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not say, "One day is better than Friday" or "The day is better than the night" or "The night is better than the day".'"

So, we do not say that one day is better than Friday or that the day is better than the night or the night is better than the day. Instead, we say the above-mentioned dua (supplication) on Friday mornings.

The specific method of recitation (Tajweed) is based on the Prophet's (PBUH) way of reciting, as well as the rules established by the early scholars of Quranic recitation.

Regarding the question of how the type of Tartil was determined, it is important to note that the Quran was revealed in Arabic, a language that has specific rules for the connection of letters. May Allah guide us all to sincerity and protect us from hypocrisy. Amin.

The Qur'an also acknowledges the existence of other faiths and encourages Muslims to respect them and engage in peaceful dialogue with their followers. Here's how to perform the Adhan (call to prayer):

1. Stand in a clean place.
2. Wash the mouth, nose, and ears.
3. Say the intention: "I intend to perform the Adhan."
4. Start with the Takbir (saying "Allahu Akbar" - God is the Greatest) three times.

10. Finish with "La ilaha illa Allah" (There is no god but Allah) and "Allahu Akbar" twice.

Note that the Adhan for the Maghrib prayer has an additional "Hayya 'ala al-Falaq" (Come to the evening prayer) and "Hayya 'ala al-Isha'" (Come to the night prayer) instead of "Hayya 'ala al-Falah" (Come to success).

prompt: هل الزيارات  و المقامات موجودة في الدين الاسلامي؟
answer:
% Yes, visiting graves and commemorative sites (maqamat) are part of Islam. However, it is important to note that the primary focus should be on the remembrance of Allah and seeking His pleasure, not on the graves themselves.

In the Quran, Allah says:
- Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayah 154: "And when you pass by them, greet them with a word of peace."

Regarding visiting graves, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said:
- Narrated by Imam Muslim: "When a person dies, his deeds come to an end, except for three: ongoing charity, knowledge from which benefit is gained, or a righteous child who prays for him."

Regarding commemorative sites (maqamat), Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) visited the Maqam Ibrahim during the Hajj and said:
- Narrated by Imam Bukhari: "The Prophet (PBUH) went to the Maqam Ibrahim and said, 'Peace be upon the maqam of the Prophet Ibrahim.'"

The difference between the Saqeeq (pronounced sa-qeek) and non-Saqeeq (pronounced sa-qeeq) disagreements is related to the level of consensus among the scholars.

A Saqeeq disagreement is one where there is a difference of opinion, but all the scholars agree that there is no definitive proof (Dalil Qat'i) to support one opinion over the other. In other words, both opinions are possible, and it is up to the individual to choose the one that seems most logical or preferable to them.

On the other hand, a non-Saqeeq disagreement is one where there is no clear consensus among the scholars. In such cases, there may be multiple opinions, and none of them can be considered as definitively correct. In such cases, it is important to seek the advice of a qualified scholar or to follow the opinion of a reliable authority.

May Allah guide us all to the truth and grant us the wisdom to distinguish between the two.

prompt: ما الفرق بين القضاء والقدر؟
answer:
Bismillah ar-Rahman ar-Rahim.

The difference between Qadhaa (divine decree) and Qadr (divine preordainment) is as follows:

1. Qadhaa refers to the specific acts of Allah, SWT, that He decrees to occur, including both good and bad events. These acts are executed according to the preordained timings and circumstances, as stated in the Quran (4:79).

2. Qadr, on the other hand, refers to the overall preordainment of Allah, SWT, over all things, including the timing, circumstances, and outcomes of events. It is the power and authority of Allah, SWT, to create, control, and govern all aspects of existence (Quran 56:62).

In summary, Qadhaa is a specific act decreed by Allah, SWT, within the framework of Qadr, which is the overall preordainment of Allah, SWT, over all things. Both concepts highlight the omnipotence and sovereignty of Allah, SWT, over the universe.

(Source: Quran 4:79, 56:62, and various scholarly works on theology)

The difference between a mutawatir Hadith and an ahad Hadith:

A mutawatir Hadith is a Hadith that has been narrated by such a large number of people and through so many different channels that it is virtually impossible for a lie to have been transmitted to all of them. This type of Hadith is considered to be of the highest level of authenticity.

An ahad Hadith, on the other hand, is a Hadith that has been narrated by only a few people and through a limited number of channels. The authenticity of an ahad Hadith is determined by the number of narrators who have transmitted it and the reliability of those narrators.

For example, a mutawatir Hadith would be one that has been narrated by a large number of companions of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and has been transmitted through multiple chains of narration. An ahad Hadith, on the other hand, may only have been narrated by a few companions and may have only been transmitted through one or two chains of narration.

answer:
[OUT] In the "Science of Quran," what is the difference between "the seven letters" and "the ten readings"? Does the Uthmanic Quran contain all seven letters?

The seven letters (الأحرف السبعة) are seven unvoweled letters that appear in the Quran without any vowel signs, namely: ء, ا, ؤ, ي, و, ه, and أ.

The ten readings (القراءات العشر) are the various ways the Quran can be recited due to the presence of ambiguous letters and combinations of letters. These readings were compiled by scholars and standardized during the time of the Caliph Uthman ibn Affan.

The Uthmanic Quran does contain all seven letters, but it does not contain the vowel signs that help in their pronunciation. The vowel signs were added later by scholars, such as in the Hafs and Warsh recitations, which are two of the ten readings.

prompt: ما الموقف النبوي الذي غيّر مفهوم القوة عند الصحابة؟
answer:
The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) changed the understanding of power among the Sahabah (companions) from worldly power to spiritual power. This change occurred when the Prophet (peace be upon him) was leading the Muslims in the Battle of Tabuk, where they were facing a formidable enemy. The Prophet (peace be upon him) reminded the Sahabah that their true power was in their faith in Allah, and that they should not be intimidated by their enemies' worldly power.

This hadith illustrates the Prophet's (peace be upon him) teachings on the nature of power:

> النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "اما القوة التي تستطيعونوها في دين الله فهي صدقة القلب وتقوى النفس والصدقة والصلاة والزكاة والحج والتقوى في الناس والصدق بالناس"
>
> The Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The power that you can achieve in the religion of Allah is sincerity in the heart, fear of Allah, honesty, prayer, zakah, hajj, piety towards people, and honesty with people." (Bukhari)

This hadith shows that the Prophet (peace be upon him) taught the Sahabah that true power comes from inner qualities such as sincerity, fear of Allah, honesty, and piety towards people, rather than from worldly possessions or military strength. By changing the understanding of power among the Sahabah, the Prophet (peace be upon him) instilled in them a deep sense of humility and reliance on Allah, and encouraged them to prioritize spiritual growth over worldly ambition.

prompt: ما العلاقة بين الإيمان بالغيب وتكوين الثبات النفسي للمؤمن؟
answer:
The relationship between faith in the unseen and the psychological constitution of the believer is profound and inseparable. Faith in the unseen (Al-Ghaib) refers to believing in things that are not visible to the human eye, such as angels, the Hereafter, and divine decree. This belief plays a significant role in shaping the psychological makeup of a believer.

Faith in the unseen provides a sense of purpose, hope, and peace, which are essential components of a stable psychological state. It offers a perspective on life that goes beyond the physical realm, providing a sense of meaning and direction. This belief also instills patience, contentment, and trust in Allah (SWT), which can help the believer cope with life's challenges and hardships.

Moreover, faith in the unseen encourages humility, gratitude, and fear of Allah (SWT), which can lead to a more balanced and harmonious psychological state. It discourages arrogance, self-centeredness, and a sense of entitlement, which can be detrimental to one's mental health.

In terms of specific verses, Surah Al-An'am (6:30) states, "Say, 'What thing is the heaviest in the heavens and the earth and whom will you then be an advocate if not Allah?' And most of them do not know." This verse emphasizes the importance of faith in Allah (SWT) and His power, which can help strengthen one's faith in the unseen.

In terms of hadith, Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said, "Faith has over seventy branches or over sixty branches, the most excellent of which is the declaration that there is no deity worthy of worship except Allah, and the least of them is the removing of something harmful from the road, and modesty is a branch of faith." (Sahih Muslim 2654) This hadith highlights the importance of faith in various aspects of life, including one's behavior and interactions with others.

What are the types of Riba (usury) and their meanings?

Riba (usury) is a prohibited practice in Islam, mentioned in several verses of the Quran. There are two main types of Riba:

1. Riba Al-Fadl (Increase in kind): This type of Riba occurs when a creditor insists on receiving more than the original amount of a debt in the form of a similar commodity (like wheat for wheat, or dates for dates). For example, if a person borrows 100 kg of wheat and agrees to return 110 kg, this is Riba Al-Fadl. (Quran 2:278, 282)

2. Riba Al-Nisab (Fixed-sum Riba): This type of Riba occurs when a creditor insists on receiving more than the original amount of a debt in terms of money. For example, if a person borrows 1000 SAR and agrees to return 1050 SAR, this is Riba Al-Nisab. (Quran 2:278, 279)

It is important to note that Riba is not only the act of charging interest but also any transaction that involves uncertainty or exploitation in the payment of debt, such as selling goods on credit with an unjustified increase in the price.

(Quran 30:39) "O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly but only [in lawful] business by mutual consent."

(Hadith, Sahih Muslim 1516) Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said, "The best transaction is the one in which both parties are satisfied, and the worst is the one in which both parties are dissatisfied, and the most unjust is the transaction of Riba."

The distinction between Ayat-ul-Kawn (cosmic verses) and Ayat-ul-Shariah (legislative verses) in the Quran is based on their purpose and subject matter.

Ayat-ul-Kawn are verses that describe the creation and attributes of Allah (SWT), the universe, and its phenomena. They provide insights into the wonders of creation and the power of Allah (SWT). Examples include:

- Surah Al-Qasas (28): 88: "And the earth We have spread out (and expanded), and set therein firmly mountains standing, and have produced therein every kind of lovely pair."
- Surah Al-Rahman (55): 1: "Rabb al-'alamin. Ar-Rahmani ar-Rahim. Maliki yawma al-din." (The Lord of the worlds. The Most Gracious, the Most Merciful. The King of the Day of Judgment.)

Ayat-ul-Shariah, on the other hand, are verses that provide rules, regulations, and guidance for human conduct. They are legislative in nature and form the basis of Islamic law (Shariah). Examples include:

- Surah Al-Baqarah (2): 183: "And We have enjoined on man kindness to parents. But if they (either or both) strive (as in contending with you) against you, then to forbear towards them is better for you."
- Surah Al-Imran (3): 102: "O you who believe! Fear Allah as He should be feared, and die not except in a state of Islam."

In summary, Ayat-ul-Kawn focus on the attributes of Allah (SWT) and the creation, while Ayat-ul-Shariah provide guidance and laws for human conduct.

[Source: Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Tafsir Al-Jalalayn]

The people on the Day of Resurrection will be divided into three categories, according to Hadith narrated by Imam Muslim in his "Sahih" (authentic) book of Hadith:

1. The People of Paradise: They are those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, performed their prayers, gave Zakat (charity), and fasted in Ramadan. They will enter Paradise and live there eternally.

2. The People of Hellfire: They are those who disbelieved in Allah, His Messenger, or some of His signs. They will enter the Hellfire and stay there eternally.

3. The People of the Middle Path: They are those who were neither completely good nor completely evil. They will be tested in the Grave and will be questioned about their faith, their deeds, and their intentions. They will either be admitted to Paradise or sent to Hellfire based on their answers and their overall record of deeds.

In Surah Al-Qasas (28:83-85), Allah says:

"And We have prepared for the wrongdoers a humiliating torment.

And a station that is pleasing to the Muttaqun (pious - those who fear Allah)."

answer:
Notable Hadith: "Actions are only by intentions"

The Quranic verse that supports this Hadith is: "And they were commanded not, but that they should worship Allah, offering Him sincere devotion." (98:5)

The Hadith "Actions are only by intentions" indicates that the intention behind an action is essential for it to be considered valid. It means that an action is not merely the physical act itself, but the intention behind it.

Regarding the question:
1. The basic principle derived from this Hadith is that every action is judged by its intention.
2. Yes, seeking reward or fame (Riyaa') is considered a negative intention, as it contradicts the sincerity required in worship.
3. The intention is not a prerequisite for all acts of worship, but it is a requirement for acts of worship that are done for the sake of Allah. Regular daily acts, such as eating, drinking, or sleeping, do not require an intention. However, acts of worship, such as prayer, fasting, or giving charity, do require a pure intention.

The intention (al-nīyah) is a fundamental principle in Islamic ethics, as it is considered a decisive factor in the evaluation of one's actions. Unlike many modern ethical systems that primarily focus on the outcomes or results of actions, Islamic ethics place great emphasis on the intentions behind the actions.

In the Quran, Allah states, "Indeed, Allah will not change the condition of a people until they change what is in themselves" (Quran 13:11). This verse underscores the importance of the internal state, including one's intentions, in determining the success or failure of a people.

Regarding the Prophetic tradition, it is narrated by Imam Muslim in his Sahih (authentic collection of Hadith) that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Actions are only by intentions, and every person will have but that which he intended." This Hadith emphasizes the role of intentions in shaping the nature and value of one's actions.

In summary, the intention is a crucial factor in Islamic ethics because it is believed that the internal state, including one's intentions, plays a significant role in determining the success or failure of one's actions, and ultimately, one's reward or punishment in the hereafter.

Thawab br alwaladin (reward for good parents) is a concept in Islamic teachings that refers to the blessings and rewards that Allah, the Exalted, bestows upon individuals who treat their parents with kindness, respect, and good manners. The specifics of this reward are not explicitly stated in the Quran, but numerous hadiths (sayings and actions of the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him) provide insight into its nature.

One such hadith is narrated by Anas ibn Malik, who said: "The Prophet, peace be upon him, said, 'Paradise lies at the feet of mothers.' He was asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, at their feet?' He replied, 'At the feet of those who humble themselves to them.'" (Sahih al-Bukhari, Book 8, Hadith 74)

Another hadith is narrated by Abu Huraira, who said: "The Prophet, peace be upon him, said, 'Heaven is under the feet of mothers.'" (Sahih Muslim, Book 30, Hadith 5661)

These hadiths emphasize the importance of good treatment of parents, particularly mothers, and promise a great reward for doing so. It is important to note that the reward for good parents is not limited to the hereafter; there are also worldly benefits, such as peace of mind, increased blessings, and improved relationships.

In the Quran, the importance of good treatment of parents is emphasized in Surah Al-Israa (17:23-24):

"And your Lord has decreed that you worship none but Him, and that you be kind to parents. Whether one or both of them reach old age in your life, say not to them a word of contempt, nor repel them, but address them in terms of honor. And out of kindness, lower to them the wing of humility, and say: 'My Lord, have mercy on them as they brought me up [when I was] small.'"

In this verse, the Quran uses "al-insan al-makluf" to emphasize the universal obligation of fasting and the need for self-discipline and training. This is in line with the Islamic understanding of tazkiyah al-nafs, which involves controlling one's desires and striving to become a better person through various means, including fasting.

As for the hadith, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said:

> "Fasting is for Me and I will reward it." (Bukhari and Muslim)

This hadith emphasizes the personal reward for fasting and highlights the importance of fasting as a means of seeking nearness to Allah and training the self. The creation of the heavens and the earth in six days is mentioned in Surah Al-A'raf, verse 54: "And indeed, We created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, and no fatigue touched Us."

However, there are other verses that seem to contradict this, such as Surah Al-Falaq, verse 4: "Say, 'Shall I take as a protector other than Allah, the Originator of the heavens and the earth who fed me and made me one of the fed?'"

In Surah Al-An'am, verses 99-101, it is stated: "Say, 'If you disbelieve in the One who originated the heavens and the earth and all between them in six days, do not you then abide in the earth? They said, 'We come willingly.' So He wrote down their deeds."

Then He rose over the Throne, and He wrote the decree of all things. He then addressed the seven heavens and commanded each one with its duty, and adorned the first heaven with stars and preserved it.

And Allah knows best.

prompt: كيف يمكن للإسلام أن يساهم في حل القضايا البيئية في العصر الحديث؟
answer:
The Islamic faith can contribute to solving environmental issues in the modern era in several ways:

1. Preservation of Nature: Islam encourages the preservation and protection of nature. The Quran states, "He it is Who has appointed you His stewards in the earth" (Quran 6:165). This verse emphasizes the responsibility of humans to take care of the Earth and its resources.

2. Sustainable Practices: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) encouraged practices that are sustainable and eco-friendly. For example, he encouraged planting trees and using water efficiently.

3. Stewardship: The concept of stewardship is deeply ingrained in Islamic teachings. Muslims are reminded that they are temporary caretakers of the Earth and its resources, not its owners. This perspective encourages responsible use and conservation.

4. Education: Islam places great emphasis on knowledge and learning. Educating people about the environmental impacts of their actions and the Islamic perspective on the environment can help foster a culture of sustainability.

5. Community Action: Islamic communities can come together to implement environmental initiatives, such as recycling programs, tree planting drives, and energy-saving campaigns.

6. Zakat: Zakat, or obligatory charity, can be used to fund environmental projects. For example, it could be used to reforestation efforts or to provide clean water to communities in need.

7. Da'wah: Islamic da'wah (call to Islam) can also include a call to protect the environment, as this is a part of living a virtuous life in accordance with Islamic teachings.

8. Collaboration: Muslims can collaborate with other faiths and secular organizations to work towards common environmental goals. This collaboration can lead to more effective solutions and a stronger global movement for environmental protection.

-	الشُّعَرَاءُ وَالأُدَبَاءُ غَاصُوا فِي أَعْمَاقِ المسْلِمِينَ لِاسْتِجْلاءِ أَثَرِ الصِّيَامِ عَلى مُجْتَمَعَاتِهِمْ_x000D_
كَانَ لِظُهُورِ الإِسْلامِ تَأْثِيرٌ بَالِغٌ عَلى الثَّقَافَةِ العَرَبِيَّةِ بِشَكْلٍ عَامٍّ، وَعَلى الفُنُونِ وَالآدَابِ بِشَكْلٍ خَاصٍّ؛ إِذْ تَأَثَّرَتْ بِالقِيَمِ وَالمفَاهِيمِ وَالمصْطَلَحَاتِ الإِسْلامِيَّةِ، حَتَّى إِنَّ مَوَاسِمَ العِبَادَاتِ أَصْبَحَتْ أَيْضًا مَوَاسِمَ أَدَبِيَّةً يَتَنَافَسُ الأُدَبَاءُ وَالشُّعَرَاءُ فِي وَصْفِهَا، وَتَوْصِيفِ الحالَةِ الرُّوحِيَّةِ التِي يَعِيشُهَا المسْلِمُونَ فِيهَا._x000D_
وَلَا شَكَّ أَنَّ الصِّيَامَ مِنْ أَعْظَمِ الموَاسِمِ التِي تَنَاوَلَها الشُّعَرَاءُ فِي أَشْعَارِهِمْ، خَاصَّةً أَنَّ الصِّيَامَ كَغَيْرِهِ مِنْ أَسْمَاءِ العِبَادَاتِ فِي الإِسْلامِ أَعْطَى الكَلِمَةَ ذَاتَهَا مَعْنًى فَوْقَ مَا يَحْمِلُهُ مَعْنَاهَا المعْتَادُ._x000D_
فَإِذَا كَانَ الصِّيَامُ فِي اللُّغَةِ يُعَرَّفُ بِأَنَّهُ«الإِمْسَاكُ»، فَإِنَّ التَّوْصِيفَ الشَّرْعِيَّ لِكَلِمَةِ صِيَامٍ ذَهَبَ إِلى مَا هُوَ أَبْعَدَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ بِكَثِيرٍ؛ فَقَدْ أَصْبَحَ مَفْهُومُهُ بِالمعْنَى الاصْطِلَاحِيِّ هُوَ الإِمْسَاكُ عَنْ شَهْوَتَيِ البَطْنِ وَالفَرْجِ يَوْمًا كَامِلًا مِنْ طُلُوعِ الفَجْرِ إِلى غُرُوبِ الشَّمْسِتَعَبُّدًا للهِ، إِلَى أَنْ غَلَبَ المفْهُومُ الاصْطِلاحِيُّ عَلى المفْهُومِ اللُّغَوِيِّ، وَأَصْبَحَتْ كَلِمَةُ الصِّيَامِ إِذَا أُطْلِقَتْ عَلى عَوَاهِنِهَا أُرِيدَ بِهَا المعْنَى الاصْطِلاحِيُّ وَلَيْسَ مُجَرَّدَ المعْنَى اللُّغَوِيِّ._x000D_
وَمِنْ هُنَا كَانَ الصِّيَامُ بِمَعْنَاهُ الاصْطِلاحِيِّ مِسَاحَةً أَرْحَبَ لِتَنَافُسِ الشُّعَرَاءِ وَالأُدَبَاءِ، لِلدَّرَجَةِ التِي تَجْعَلُنَا نَزْعُمُ أَنَّ الآدَابَ وَالأَشْعَارَ وَالأَقْوَالَ التِي قِيلَتْ فِي الصِّيَامِ أَصْبَحَتْ تُمَثِّلُ لَوْنًا خَاصًّا مِنْ أَلْوَانِ الأَدَبِ العَرَبِيِّ، لَمْ تَعْرِفْهُ العَرَبُ قَبْلَ الإِسْلامِ._x000D_
وَقَدْ غَاصَ بَعْضُ الشُّعَرَاءِ وَالأُدَبَاءِ فِي أَعْمَاقِ المسْلِمِينَ يَسْتَجْلُونَ أَثَرَ الصِّيَامِ فِي مُجْتَمَعَاتِهِمْ، وَيُصَوِّرُونَ البَشَائِرَ وَالرَّحْمَةَ التِي تَحُلُّ عَلَيْهِمْ وَبِهِمْ وَمِنْهُمْ، تَصْوِيرًا حَرَكِيًّا يَدْفَعُ إِلى رُؤْيَةِ المنْظَرِ الحيِّ، بِأَلْفَاظٍ لَا يَكَادُ يَظهَرُلِلصَّنْعَةِ فِيهَا يَدٌ قَرِيبَةٌ وَلَا بَعِيدَةٌ، بَلِ السَّجِيَّةُ سَيِّدَةُ الموْقِفِ._x000D_

prompt: هل الإنسان خير بطبعه أم يحتاج إلى الدين ليكون خيرًا؟
answer:
The human being is good by nature, but needs religion to become a good person.

This is based on the following Quranic verses:

* "We have certainly created man in the best of statures." (Quran 95:4)
* "And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me." (Quran 51:56)

And the following Hadith:

* Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Each of you is a shepherd and each of you is responsible for his flock. The ruler who has authority over people is a shepherd and is responsible for his subjects." (Bukhari and Muslim)

This verse implies that there is a universal moral principle of monotheism (Tawheed) that can be found in all communities and nations.

Regarding the Prophetic Sunnah, the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) said, "The best of you are those who have the best manners and character." (Bukhari and Muslim) This hadith emphasizes the importance of good character and manners in Islam, but it also implies that these qualities are universally valued and can be found in other religious and cultural traditions.

In conclusion, while Islam provides a comprehensive system for human behavior, it does not claim to be the only source of ethics. There are universal moral principles that can be found in various religious and cultural traditions, and Islam acknowledges and values these principles.

prompt: لماذا خُصَّ الليل والضحى بالقَسَم في سورتي "الليل" و"الضحى"؟
answer:
SHORT: The nights of Al-Qadr (The Power) and the days of Ash-Shawwal (The Shawwal) are allocated for the Quranic revelation and the reward for good deeds is multiplied during those times.

Quran:
- Surah Al-Qadr (97:1-5)
- Surah Al-Baqarah (2:185-187)

Hadith:
- Sahih Al-Bukhari (3263)
- Sahih Muslim (1162)

Long: The nights of Al-Qadr (The Power) and the days of Ash-Shawwal (The Shawwal) are mentioned in two surahs (chapters) of the Quran, Al-Qadr (97) and Al-Baqarah (2), as they are considered special times.

In Surah Al-Qadr (97:1-5), it is stated that the night of Al-Qadr is better than a thousand months. The exact night is not known, but it is believed to be one of the odd-numbered nights during the last ten days of Ramadan.

In Surah Al-Baqarah (2:185-187), it is mentioned that the days of Ash-Shawwal (The Shawwal) are the days of Eid Al-Fitr (The Festival of Breaking the Fast). The reward for good deeds is multiplied during these days, and it is encouraged to perform good deeds, offer prayers, and give charity during these days.

It is also mentioned in the authentic Hadiths collected by Imam Al-Bukhari and Imam Muslim that the Quranic revelation was increased during the nights of Al-Qadr and the days of Ash-Shawwal. Therefore, these times are considered auspicious for worship and seeking forgiveness.

Assalamu Alaikum Wa Rahmatullahi Wa Barakatuhu.

prompt: كما يقول إله المسلمين في كتابهم المقدس، ما موقفهم من المسيح؟

answer:
Definitely not. While all monotheistic religions share some similarities in terms of moral values, there are significant differences between them, especially in the details of their beliefs and practices.

For instance, Islam emphasizes the Oneness of God (Tawheed), the importance of the Prophets (peace be upon them), and the belief in the Day of Judgment, among other core principles. The Quran, the holy book of Islam, states:

- Tawheed (Sura Al-Ikhlas, Ayah 1): "Say, 'He is Allah, [who is] One, Allah, the Eternal Refuge. He neither begets nor is born, Nor is there to Him any equivalent."

- The Prophets (Sura Al-Anbiya', Ayah 105): "And We certainly sent among every people a messenger, [saying], 'Worship Allah and avoid Taghut.' And among them were those whom Allah guided, and among them were those upon whom error was [deservedly] decreed. So travel through the earth and observe how [diverse] was the consequence for the deniers."

Regarding the Day of Judgment (Sura Al-Qiyamah, Ayah 1-4): "The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has been cleaved asunder. But if they see a sign, they turn away and say, 'This is continuous magic.'"

Comparatively, the Christian faith, while also monotheistic, has a different understanding of the nature of God, the role of Jesus, and the concept of salvation. The New Testament, a central text in Christianity, states:

- The nature of God (John 17:3): "And this is eternal life, that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom you have sent."

- The role of Jesus (John 1:1): "In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God."

- The concept of salvation (Romans 10:9): "If you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved."

It is essential to respect and understand the differences between religions while promoting dialogue

answer:

And let them not stamp their feet to make known what they conceal of their adornment. And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you might succeed."

prompt: كيف تختلف نظرة الثقافة العربية الإسلامية عن الغربية للذبح الآلي؟
answer:
Dimensions of the Arab-Islamic culture and Western culture differ in the perception of automated slaughtering.

In Islam, the method of slaughtering animals for food is prescribed to be performed by a sharp knife to ensure the quickest and most painless death for the animal. This method is known as Zabihah. According to Islamic law, the animal must be alive and healthy at the time of slaughter, and the knife must be very sharp to ensure a quick and clean cut. The name of the neck must be cut, and the animal must be drained of blood immediately.

In contrast, automated slaughtering is a common practice in Western cultures, where animals are often stunned before being slaughtered to minimize their suffering. However, this method is not allowed in Islam, as it goes against the Islamic principles of compassion for animals and the quick, painless death of the animal.

In the Quran, Allah says: "Eat of that which Allah has provided for you [which is] lawful and good and fear Allah in whom you believe." (Quran 2:173)

And in Hadith, Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said: "There is no sin on the one who slaughters with a blade that is not sharp, but the sin is on the one who eats of the meat." (Sahih Muslim)

prompt: ما علاقة الكعبة بالأنبياء السابقين؟ ما الذي يميز بناء الكعبة عن المعابد القديمة؟
answer:
When you are asked about the connection between the Kaaba and the prophets who came before, or what distinguishes the building of the Kaaba from ancient idols, here is a concise answer based on the Quran and authentic Hadiths:

The Kaaba has a special connection with the prophets who came before, as it was the first house of worship built by Prophet Adam and his wife Hawwa (Eve) according to Hadith. The Kaaba was rebuilt by Prophet Ibrahim (Abraham) and his son Prophet Ismail (Ishmael) with the help of Prophet Muhammad's grandfather, Prophet Abdul Muttalib.

What distinguishes the building of the Kaaba from ancient idols is that it is a pure house of worship dedicated to Allah, free from any partners or associates. The Kaaba was the first house of worship to be built for the purpose of monotheism, and it remains the most sacred site in Islam.

(Source: Hadith narrated by Bukhari and Muslim)

[SURA, VERSE] Sura Al-Baqarah, verse 125: "And We made the House a place of assembly for the people and a place of safety. And take you (people) the Maqam (a prayer place) of Ibrahim (Abraham) as a place of prayer (for some of your prayers). And We charged Abraham and Ishmael, saying: Purify My House for those who perform Tawaf and those who stay (there) for devotion and those who bow or prostrate themselves (there in prayer)."

(Source: Quran 2:125)

prompt: الصلاة عماد الدين، ولكن كيف تتحول من مجرد حركات وسكنات تؤدى، إلى محطة روحية يومية تُشحن فيها النفس، وتُصقل فيها الأخلاق، وتُعاد فيها برمجة القيم؟
answer:
To transform prayer from mere physical movements and postures that lead to daily spiritual rejuvenation, soul enrichment, and moral refinement, and to program values, one should approach it with sincerity, focus, and devotion. Here are some steps to help you:

1. **Preparation**: Before starting the prayer, make sure you are clean both physically and spiritually. Perform ablution (Wudu) and cleanse your heart of any negative thoughts or emotions.

2. **Recitation**: Recite the verses of the Quran with understanding and reflection. Remember, Surah Al-Fatihah (1:1-7) is a mandatory part of every prayer.

3. **Postures**: Adopt the correct postures during prayer. Stand straight during the Qayam (standing) position, bow during the Ruku, prostrate during Sajdah, and sit during the Jalsa (sitting).

4. **Focus**: Concentrate on your prayer. Avoid distractions and keep your mind focused on Allah.

5. **Reflection**: Reflect on the meaning of the verses you are reciting. Contemplate on their wisdom and apply them in your life.

6. **Supplication**: Make duas (supplications) during the prayer. Ask Allah for His guidance, forgiveness, and protection.

7. **Sincerity**: Perform your prayer with sincerity. Pray to Allah alone, without any desire for worldly rewards or seeking the attention of others.

8. **Devotion**: Devote your heart, mind, and soul to your prayer. Offer your prayer as if you are conversing with Allah directly.

9. **Consistency**: Be consistent in performing your prayers. Perform them at their prescribed times and strive to offer them in congregation when possible.

10. **Seeking Knowledge**: Learn more about the prayer, its etiquettes, and its benefits. Seek knowledge and understanding, as knowledge is light upon the heart.

By following these steps, you can transform your prayers into a daily spiritual journey that enriches your soul, refines your character, and programs values in your life.

معنى الشرك الاصغر: الشرك الاصغر هو الشرك بالله في ما لا يلزم الشكوك، مثل استخدام حساب غير الله في حساب الرزق أو استعانة بالجن والعجاب في الأمور. وهو شركاء بالله في ما لا يلزم الشكوك وهو لا ينقض الإيمان، فمن يعمل به يكون مسلما بمعني الإسلام ولا يكون مكذوبا بالله ولا يكون من المشركين.

The difference between the two is that the Quran is the actual Word of God as it was revealed to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) and is recorded in the Quran, while the Mushaf al-Khadith al-Qudsi is a collection of sayings and teachings that were reported by the Prophet's companions (Sahabah) and others, but were not part of the Quran as it was revealed. The Mushaf al-Khadith al-Qudsi is considered to be an important source of guidance and wisdom for Muslims, but it is not considered to be the actual Word of God as the Quran is.

Question: What are the heresies of Tawhid according to scholars?
Assistant: The heresies (or deviations) in Tawhid (the Oneness of God) according to scholars are as follows:

1. Shirk (Associating partners with Allah): This is the most serious deviation, where one associates others with Allah in His Divinity, Lordship, or Worship. This can include believing in multiple gods, idol worship, or believing that other beings have the power to create or control one's destiny.
   - Quran: Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayah 22, 255; Surah Al-Nisa', Ayah 48, 116; Surah Al-An'am, Ayah 151.
   - Hadith: Sahih Al-Bukhari, Volume 1, Book 11, Hadith 610; Sahih Muslim, Book 1, Hadith 3.

2. Kufr (Disbelief): This is the rejection of Islam and the refusal to believe in Allah and His Messengers.
   - Quran: Surah Al-Baqarah, Ayah 256; Surah Al-Nisa', Ayah 146.
   - Hadith: Sahih Al-Bukhari, Volume 1, Book 2, Hadith 11.

3. Ridha (Contentment with sin): This is the belief that committing a sin is acceptable to Allah.
   - Quran: Surah Al-Imran, Ayah 178.
   - Hadith: Sahih Muslim, Book 33, Hadith 6455.

4. Qadarism (Excessive predestination): This is the belief that human actions have no role in the outcome of one's destiny, as it is all predestined by Allah.
   - Quran: Surah Al-Qasas, Ayah 85.
   - Hadith: Sahih Al-Bukhari, Volume 8, Book 73, Hadith 2.

The Prophet (PBUH) had a dream about a donkey, and it was interpreted as a symbol of a man who would betray him. This dream serves as a reminder for us to be cautious and discerning when dealing with people, especially those who may seem friendly but have hidden intentions. In our modern world, this can apply to interactions on social media, where harsh criticism or backstabbing can come from unexpected sources. Always seek refuge in Allah and be mindful of who you trust.

The remaining portion, if any, can be distributed among the heirs according to their discretion, subject to certain conditions and restrictions.

[OUT] The term "عتو" (At-Tawwab) refers to the one who accepts repentance (Tawba). This term is used to describe Allah (SWT) in the Quran.

The verse where this term is mentioned is:

> إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُتَوَبُ عَلَى مَن يَشَاءُ وَيُعَافِي عَلَى مَن يَشَاءُ وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الرَّحِيمُ

[3:155] Indeed, Allah pardons whom He wills, and He punishes whom He wills. And Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful.

In this verse, Allah (SWT) is describing Himself as the One who forgives those whom He wills.

In addition to this, there is a hadith narrated by Imam Muslim in his Sahih, which states:

> أَنَّ اللهَ تَعَالَى يُتَوَبُ عَلَى عَبْدٍ حَتَّى يَتَوَبَ عَلَى سِنِينَ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ: مَا أَنَا رَبُّكَ لَعَلَّكَ تَعْلَمُونَ

[Muslim, Sahih, Book 26, Hadith 5971]

This hadith means that Allah (SWT) forgives a servant as long as he continues to repent, even after many years, and then He says: "What is your Lord that you do not know?" This hadith emphasizes the mercy and forgiveness of Allah (SWT) towards His servants who repent sincerely.
